To this end, we define three parameters that characterize bichromatic states of polarization and span the Kummer shape, the bichromatic counterpart of the Poincaré sphere. We find that, under certain conditions, full Kummer beams can exhibit skyrmionic textures with a Skyrme number that depends not only on the topological charges but also on the frequencies. These beams can also exhibit emergent behavior upon propagation, including robust, higher-order-like structures and a propagation-invariant Skyrme number over a wide range of beam-waist selections.

items.title: Hydrodynamic modeling of liquid metal field emitter deformation under combined RF and DC magnetic fields
items.summary: Radio-frequency (RF) breakdowns, also known as vacuum (or electrical) arcs and breakdowns, or electrical discharges, have been studied for over decades, but the mechanisms of the RF breakdown are still questionable. This phenomenon reduces the stability of the beam, damages the RF cavities, and thus limits the achievable accelerating field in the particle accelerator. In the case of Muon Collider, the RF cavities have to withstand an electric field of the order of multi tens of MV/m and a DC magnetic field of a few tens of teslas, with a minimum rate of RF breakdown. Different models have been proposed, and some important factors that could lead to the RF breakdown have been identified, such as the field emission current, irregularity of the surface , presence of hot particles on the surface and the role of the DC magnetic field. In this paper, we give insights to the mechanism of RF breakdowns using a hydrodynamic and a magnetohydrodynamic approach, focusing on understanding the forces that deform the liquid copper emitter. We found that if the local RF electric field is sufficiently high, it could provoke the emission of hot copper droplets into the cavity. Our simulations use the computational fluid dynamics module, the magnetic and electric field module, and the level set method in the COMSOL software to simulate the behavior of a copper liquid emitter with the Navier-Stokes equation under the influence of the pressure radiation, and the surface tension force.

items.title: Towards end-to-end optimization in multimaterial 3D printing
items.summary: Multimaterial 3D printing enables the fabrication of functionally graded components, but optimizing their spatial material distribution alongside structural topology remains a formidable challenge due to high-dimensional design spaces and complex constitutive modeling. Using neural network constitutive laws in topology optimization requires their tangents and design sensitivities, which current approaches obtain by automatic differentiation through the network or derivation by hand. This paper combines sparsification, which reduces a trained physics-augmented neural network to a compact, interpretable closed-form law, with symbolic differentiation, enabling an end-to-end workflow from a new continuously varying multimaterial system to its mechanical simulation and design. By extracting closed-form, composition-aware hyperelastic constitutive laws from sparsified neural networks trained on experimental data, this approach facilitates exact symbolic differentiation of the terms required by the adjoint state method implemented with FEniCSx, circumventing the bottlenecks of applying neural network constitutive models in analysis and optimization. This pipeline is deployed on soft robotic gripper applications, demonstrating continuous composition optimization for highly anisotropic contact responses, and the concurrent optimization of macroscopic topology and material distribution under non-failure stretch constraints. This study is a step toward replacing conventional constitutive modeling and laborious empirical prototyping, establishing interpretable machine-learning models as practical, robust design primitives for advanced multimaterial additive manufacturing.

items.title: Fast electrons and high energy photons produced in strong-field ionization of atoms as diagnostics of multi-petawatt laser beams
items.summary: We calculate numerically energy spectra and angular distributions of photoelectrons and X-ray photons emitted in the process of tunnel photoionization of argon by a focused laser beam of multi-petawatt power. By scanning the beam power and varying the degree of focusing and the field polarization, we show these distributions to be sensitive both to the peak laser intensity and to the field configuration in the focal spot. Investigated parameters of the laser beam correspond to those of several recently commissioned lasers of multi-petawatt power. These findings, in line with the earlier reported proposals, provide a basis for the development of a reliable ionization diagnostics of extremely intense laser fields.

items.title: Localization Landscapes based on the Green's Matrix of Non-Hermitian Optical Scattering Systems
items.summary: The Filoche--Mayboroda (FM) localization landscape predicts where the spatially localized modes of a self-adjoint elliptic operator reside without diagonalizing it, but the construction fails for the complex, non-normal Green's matrix G of an open scattering array of electric dipoles. We propose three real-valued, positive landscapes built from the Feinberg--Zee hermitization of G: a regularized Gramian inverse (Gram), the diagonal Schur block that carries the Metz--Neri--Rogers spectral density (SY), and the full hermitized inverse contracted against a uniform source (TM) or an isotropic polarization pair (TE) (Herm). The three form a progression from spectrum-blind to fully hermitization-faithful, agree in the limit $z\to 0$, and diverge where it matters: at nonzero spectral shift SY resolves modes that Gram collapses, and Herm resolves modes that SY collapses. We demonstrate the progression on random and deterministic aperiodic scattering arrays with a wide range of structural correlations, extend to the vectorial case of transverse electric polarization (TE), and provide rigorous pointwise envelope bounds for the Spec and Herm landscapes, a physical argument for the spatial compactness of long-lived modes, and a complete numerical recipe in the appendices.

items.title: Lagrangian transport driven by travelling waves in a radially deforming circular cavity
items.summary: A travelling deformation of a circular cavity wall can carry particles with the wave or against it. For two counter-propagating waves of azimuthal order $m$ and amplitudes $a$ and $b$, the leading axisymmetric component of the total (Lagrangian) drift scales with the intensity difference $S_3=|a|^2-|b|^2$. We obtain the radial profile of the azimuthal drift in closed form in the viscous limit, where the Womersley number $\mathrm{Wo}$ tends to zero, and by quadrature for any finite $\mathrm{Wo}>0$. The total drift is the sum of the Eulerian mean velocity and the Stokes drift. For radial wall motion with $m\ge2$ and unequal wave intensities, the total drift follows the stronger of the two waves throughout the interior in the viscous limit, although the Stokes drift changes sign with radius for all $\mathrm{Wo}$. For $m=2$ and large $\mathrm{Wo}$, the predicted total drift just inside a radially moving wall opposes the wave to leading order in wall amplitude. For the same travelling shape, the total drift there follows the wave when the wall material also moves tangentially to preserve local arc length to first order. For the radial wall at large $\mathrm{Wo}$, the near-wall profile consists of the planar Longuet-Higgins result and a closed-form curvature correction. At large $m$ the core rotation approaches Tuck's finite-Reynolds-number waving-sheet result. At $m=2$ and $\mathrm{Wo}^2=10$, moving-domain simulations recover the leading-order drift coefficients for both wall motions.

items.title: Perturbations in the parametrized wormhole spacetime and their related quasinormal modes
items.summary: We study electromagnetic perturbations and the associated quasinormal modes (QNMs) of parametrized static, spherically symmetric wormhole spacetimes, focusing on Damour-Solodukhin and braneworld geometries as well as their galactic extensions. Using the Bronnikov-Konoplya-Pappas (BKP) parametrization, we express the metric functions in terms of a compactified radial coordinate and characterize the spacetime through far-field and near-throat parameters. The far-field coefficients govern the asymptotic structure and post-Newtonian behaviour, while the near-throat continued-fraction expansion captures the strong-field geometry near the throat. We first apply the parametrization to isolated wormholes and identify its range of validity, showing that the non-analytic metric functions can limit the applicability of the BKP scheme. Moreover we have shown that such issues can indeed hamper the primary ringdown waveform. We then extend the framework to a galactic Damour-Solodukhin wormhole embedded in a Hernquist dark matter halo. Imposing observational bounds from the shadow of Sgr A$^*$, we constrain the galactic compactness and deformation parameters and obtain an observationally viable parametrized metric. Within the allowed parameter space, we compute the fundamental QNM frequencies using the transfer matrix method and analyze the corresponding time-domain ringdown signals. We find that the damping rate is more sensitive to galactic compactness, whereas the oscillation frequency remains comparatively stable. Although the spectral shifts are small within the shadow-allowed region, the framework provides a systematic link between geometric parametrization, shadow constraints, and dynamical response. Our results establish an observationally consistent parametrized description of wormhole perturbations for strong-field tests of horizonless compact objects.

items.title: Magnetic field induced modulation of heat transport in CrPS$_4$ probed by TaIrTe$_4$ transverse Seebeck thermometry
items.summary: Understanding and controlling heat flow in low-dimensional magnetic materials is central to thermoelectrics and spin caloritronics. One of the challenges is the absence of sensitive probes of small, field-dependent modulations in thermal transport. Here we demonstrate transverse Seebeck thermometry using exfoliated TaIrTe$_4$ as a probe of thermal conductivity modulated by an external magnetic field on a van der Waals magnet, CrPS$_4$. With a temperature gradient oriented at $45^\circ$ to its principal crystallographic axes, TaIrTe$_4$ exhibits a transverse thermopower exceeding $200~\mathrm{μV\,K^{-1}}$ for 900 nm wide and 30 $μ$m long electrodes, enabling precise detection of variations in the local temperature gradients. Exploiting this with CrPS$_4$ in a nonlocal geometry, we resolve distinct field dependent thermal conductivity changes associated with both the spin-flip and spin-flop magnetic transitions which we attribute to variations in the magnon$-$phonon coupling in CrPS$_4$. At 5 K, the transverse Seebeck response is modulated by more than 8$\%$ by an external magnetic field, demonstrating strong magnetic control of heat transport in CrPS$_4$. This all van der Waals platform offers high sensitivity to modulations of thermal conductivity and a broad adaptability to a wide range of exfoliated magnetic systems.

items.title: Future avenues for precision oscillation measurements with compact movable reactors
items.summary: No planned neutrino experiment is expected to surpass Daya Bay's precision on $\thone$. Doing so requires innovative strategies to reduce statistical and systematic uncertainties. In this study, we consider a futuristic program with a movable reactor antineutrino source placed within short distances ($L\lesssim 3\,\km$) from the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) detector. Due to the large fiducial mass of JUNO, even a relatively small reactor can produce a statistically significant number of events over a few years to probe the $\lesssim 8.7\% \,\nuebar$ disappearance set by $\thone$. We consider two possibilities: a $\mathcal{O}(20\mwth)$ microreactor in alcoves of the access tunnel to the underground laboratory, and a $\mathcal{O}(400 \mwth)$ unit on the surface. In both cases the reactor is observed by a small flux monitor detector near the source, while JUNO measures the antineutrino flux at two baselines, suppressing correlated flux and detector systematics. Using the measured Daya Bay per-isotope spectra and its covariance, we model a high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) core for the microreactor and a low-enriched uranium (LEU) core for the surface unit, and discuss various potential sources of systematic uncertainties and their impact on the precision of $\thone$. The underground microreactor could improve on JUNO's reach by a factor of three to four, to $\relsth \simeq 4\%$ over a decade, while the surface reactor would reach the present global-fit precision, $\relsth=2.5\%$, in about three years, provided the emission rate is monitored across reactor relocations to the sub-percent level.

items.title: A unified closed-form theory for elastic waves in polycrystals of any crystal symmetry
items.summary: The coherent elastic wave in random polycrystals is described by the first-order smoothing approximation, whose mass operator remains an integral evaluated only numerically. Here we derive its closed form for equiaxed, untextured polycrystals of any crystal symmetry with an exponential correlation function, giving an explicit dispersion equation at all frequencies. Unlike the integral form, which fails beyond one inverse correlation radius from the real axis, the closed form holds deep in the complex wavenumber plane, where heavily attenuated roots lie. It is compact, reproduces the dispersion equations of Stanke and Kino for cubic grains, extends them to any symmetry and contains the Born and far-field approximations as special cases. It reveals the structure of the roots and their partitions of the coherent field: three roots per polarization, one from the incident wave and one from each of the two scattering channels, without and with mode conversion. It also yields closed-form limits of their velocity, attenuation and partition in the Rayleigh, stochastic and geometric regimes, which show why a single coherent wave has been observed at long wavelengths, whereas more than one can be observed at short wavelengths. These results underpin further theory and quantitative characterization of polycrystalline microstructure.

items.title: Aggregating soft-photon recoil with a positive finite-step sampler
items.summary: We model stochastic radiation reaction by aggregating soft photons into one positive recoil, retaining the local no-emission probability and two loss moments of the crossed-field QED kernel. Unlike Gaussian diffusion, the sampler preserves one-sided energy loss. Analytical synchrotron moments expose a finite-step cooling bias, which state feedback reduces. Laser and ion-channel tests probe excessive-loss risk and directed radiation spectra, providing a practical route to stochastic particle simulations without resolving individual soft emissions.

items.title: Gravitational radiation from a particle in circular orbit around a wormhole: the nonrotating case
items.summary: In this paper, we have generalized Poisson's(1993) calculation for the case of gravitational radiation from a particle in a circular orbit around a black hole to the case of the wormhole. Considering the motion of a test particle around a Schwarzschild like wormhole and using Teukolsky formalism, we have obtained an analytical result of flux at infinity under the assumption of small velocities. Focusing on the 22-mode, we have found a novel 0.5PN order term beyond the quadrupole order, which vanishes in the black hole limit. On the other hand, all higher order terms are getting modified in such a way that they give correct correspondence in the black hole limit. We have further corroborated our results with the numerical investigations, which show that the two waveforms match well when the particle lies far from ISCO. Thus, our work provides one of the first attempts toward the study of the post-Newtonian waveforms involving wormholes (ECOs).

items.title: Nonequilibrium Statistical Mechanics: Physical Concepts & Mathematical Tools
items.summary: As anything not in equilibrium is, by definition, nonequilibrium, there is no universally agreed-upon set of topics that can constitute an exhaustive presentation of nonequilibrium statistical mechanics. At the same time, nonequilibrium statistical mechanics has transcended traditional physics to become a powerful language for complex systems. Prompted by an enthusiastic curiosity about complex systems, these cursory lecture notes attempt to elucidate some introductory concepts and techniques used in classical nonequilibrium statistical mechanics, which find successful applications not only in foundational physics, but also across other fields such as biology, ecology, economics, and sociology. Except for the specific synthesis and presentation of the material, which assumes basic familiarity with equilibrium statistical mechanics, the author claims no originality.

items.title: Simulation-pretrained autoencoders versus PCA for compressing multimode fibre transmission matrices
items.summary: Multimode optical fibres can image through a thin, flexible probe once their transmission matrix (TM) has been measured, but a TM is large and must be re-measured whenever the fibre moves. A compact model of feasible TMs would make storing and re-estimating them cheaper, so we ask how compactly TMs can be represented, and from how few measured TMs. Here we benchmark a permutation-equivariant autoencoder, pretrained on simulated fibres and adapted to measured TMs, against principal component analysis (PCA). At 62x compression, adapting the pretrained autoencoder with just two measured TMs reconstructs the TM of a 50um fibre well enough to focus light at 98% of the ideal enhancement, and it stays accurate when the TMs are shifted by 25 pixels or zoomed by 10%, which quickly degrades a linear basis. It is not, however, a better compressor: PCA is about ten times more accurate when fitted on all 163 real TMs (1.1% against 11.9% error on held-out TMs) and is already more accurate from ten. The autoencoder's value is as a prior when few or no real TMs exist: with none it reaches 29% error, against 91% for PCA fitted on the same simulation. Transfer to a different fibre is only partial. The most important extension, not yet tested, is to recover pixel-basis TMs from fewer measurements than a full TM, which would turn the pretrained prior from a compressor into a measurement-saving tool.

items.title: A photon-number-conserving multimode framework for pulse propagation dynamics across zero nonlinearity: Kerr-Raman cooperation and competition
items.summary: Raman scattering in multimode fibers shifts pulse spectra to lower frequencies and transfers photons between spatial modes. When the nonlinear coefficient changes sign within the pulse spectrum, the ordinary generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE) can give unphysical predictions. Existing photon-number-conserving formulations either treat a single mode or exclude Raman scattering. We develop a time-domain multimode GNLSE that conserves photon number, includes the full Raman response and remains well defined at the zero-nonlinearity frequency. For narrowband pulses with a constant positive nonlinear coefficient, the framework reduces to the standard multimode GNLSE with instantaneous Kerr and delayed Raman terms. We then apply the framework to three coherently excited modes whose spectra shift across the zero-nonlinearity frequency. The Kerr and Raman processes first cooperate and then compete. In the first stage, both processes transfer photons into the fundamental mode, contributing about 2\% and 43\% of the initial total photon number. In the second stage, Kerr transfer drives photons out of the fundamental mode, while Raman transfer drives photons back, contributing about $-27\%$ and $+15\%$, respectively. Consequently, the fundamental-mode photon fraction rises from 20\% to 65\% and then falls to 53\%. Kerr terms that leave the modal photon populations unchanged still reshape the fields and thereby enhance Raman transfer. Moreover, changing only the relative input phases can reverse the initial Raman-driven flow into the fundamental mode, even for identical modal spectra. Taken together, the results show how instantaneous and delayed nonlinear responses, together with intermodal phase, govern photon redistribution across zero nonlinearity.

items.title: High-Power Short-Wavelength Frequency Comb from Coherent Radiation of Uncompressed Electron Beams
items.summary: High-power frequency combs at short wavelengths would open new opportunities for precision measurements and high-resolution spectroscopy. Here, we propose a frequency comb based on coherent undulator radiation from uncompressed electron bunches. An optical frequency comb serves as the seed, establishing a common phase reference for microbunching in successive electron bunches and transferring its phase coherence to short-wavelength harmonic radiation. By exploiting interference between distinct laser-induced microbunching pathways, we reduce the sensitivity of the harmonic bunching phase to electron-beam energy fluctuations, a major challenge for maintaining interpulse coherence. Start-to-end simulations demonstrate frequency comb generation in the vacuum-ultraviolet (148 nm) and soft X-ray regimes, yielding average radiation powers of approximately 1 W and 100 mW, respectively, with approximately 6 $μ$W and 100 nW concentrated in individual comb teeth. These results establish a promising route toward high-power, phase-coherent short-wavelength frequency combs for precision spectroscopy, including searches for the nuclear transition in trapped $^{229}$Th ions.

items.title: Quantum Zeno Effect with a Superposed Measurement Schedule in Relational Time
items.summary: Motivated by the Page-Wootters construction in which time is a quantum clock reading and the global system state is stationary, we propose a quantum circuit that explores the observable consequences of treating measurement timing as a quantum degree of freedom. We place two Zeno measurement schedules of a driven qubit in a coherent superposition using a schedule qubit. We show that, for a fixed drive strength, the interference visibility between the two schedules depends only on the time offset between them, not on the number of intermediate measurements taken. Then we show that, for one schedule-readout outcome, the Zeno trend reverses, predicting a result that complements the standard Zeno probability. We propose a circuit implementation with physical memory qubits and show that measuring the memory register's joint $X$-basis parity distinguishes a coherent schedule from a classical or dephased one. We give the gate count and an error budget for a superconducting-qubit implementation. The Page-Wootters picture motivates this protocol and provides an equivalent stationary representation, although the predictions follow from the standard circuit description without requiring a relational-time interpretation. This is consistent with the Page-Wootters framework recovering standard quantum dynamics through correlations between a clock and the rest of the system.

items.title: The two-component picture of soft hadron production: Regge exchange, duality, and resonance cascades
items.summary: The fragmentation regions of soft hadronic collisions approach energy-independent limits. Benecke, Chou, Yang, and Yen stated this hypothesis of limiting fragmentation in 1969, and Feynman gave it a parton-model formulation the same year. Measurements from the CERN Intersecting Storage Rings (ISR) to the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) show this approach. Fischer and co-workers interpret the NA49 spectra from the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) as the sum of a target and a projectile component, each the decay of an excited hadronic system. This review traces the theory behind that two-component picture. It examines the hypothesis that the hadronic tools that predate quantum chromodynamics (QCD) suffice for the soft, non-perturbative domain of QCD. Regge exchange organizes the fragmentation region in triple-Regge form and supplies the diffractive mass law of the excited systems. Finite-energy sum rules and the two-component duality of Harari and Freund equate averaged towers of resonances with that exchange. Duality therefore motivates describing the excited systems in hadronic degrees of freedom. The cascade description has five predecessors, namely the fireballs of Niu, the novas of Jacob and Slansky, the clusters of Hwa, Good-Walker diffraction, and the two-stage dissociation of Hama. A companion paper (arXiv:2611.11570) assembles these pieces into HEART (Hadronic Excitations And Resonance Transitions), an event-level cascade of two-body hadronic transitions, and fits it to the NA49 data. The review closes with the fragmentation-region measurements that would separate a resonance cascade from a string, namely the isospin of forward baryons, local strangeness balance, and forward resonance signals.

items.title: How Should Candidates Be Weighted under Open-List Proportional Representation? Harmonic Weights and Dirichlet Order Statistics
items.summary: Candidates in open-list proportional representation systems are not equally prominent, and measurements that involve aggregation over candidates therefore require some form of weighting. We address the question of how those weights should be chosen. Since weights based on realized preference votes are unavailable in advance and endogenous to the electoral outcome, we seek a priori weights that depend on list position alone, and derive them as expected ordered vote shares under a probabilistic model of the division of the list vote among candidates. The natural starting point -- the uniform distribution on the simplex -- is unrealistic, as it prescribes the same degree of concentration of the vote for every list, and under it the leading candidates become more alike as lists lengthen. The other members of the symmetric Dirichlet family require a concentration parameter, which is unknown and which there is no reason to expect to be constant across countries, parties, and elections. Accordingly, we treat that parameter as random. We prove that under a scale-invariant prior restricted to lists with at least two effective candidates, the expected share of the $k$-th candidate decays as $1/k$, and we show that over the leading positions of a long list, up to one hundred of them, the resulting weights are within 1.4 to 3.4 percent, in total variation, of the harmonic weights $(k H_n)^{-1}$, where $H_n$ is the $n$-th harmonic number. No fixed value of the parameter yields similar weights. Moreover, under the uniform distribution itself, harmonic weights are exactly the normalized expected margins between consecutive candidates.

items.title: Hybrid Plasmon-Phonon Eigenmodes and Vortex States in a Graphene Ring on a Silica Substrate
items.summary: We investigate hybrid plasmon-phonon eigenmodes and localized electromagnetic vortex states in a graphene ring supported by a dispersive silica substrate. The interaction between graphene plasmons and infrared-active optical phonons of the substrate gives rise to distinct spectral branches of surface polaritons, whose dispersion characteristics are established analytically and validated by full-wave numerical simulations. Geometric confinement of these hybrid surface excitations produces spectrally separated families of localized multipolar eigenmodes with corresponding azimuthal symmetries. Particular attention is devoted to quadrupolar eigenstates, which exhibit nearly identical normalized spatial field distributions despite their substantial spectral separation and different attenuation characteristics. We demonstrate that coherent superposition of orthogonal quadrupolar field patterns gives rise to localized vortex states with opposite azimuthal phase winding. The preservation of the spatial eigenmode structure across distinct spectral branches is consistent with a quasistatic description in which the resonator geometry governs the modal symmetry, whereas the dispersive material response determines the spectral properties. These findings reveal a route toward controlling structured electromagnetic near fields through plasmon--phonon hybridization and establish a physical basis for multiband vortex states in deeply subwavelength graphene resonators.

items.title: Compact GridPix Tracking: Test Beam Performance and Detector Response Modelling
items.summary: We characterise a Timepix-based GridPix detector with a 21 mm drift length using 2.6 GeV electrons at ELSA. Tracks entering through the window at several angles are reconstructed as compact $μ$TPC tracklets, providing position and local direction from one layer. Measured angular widths are approximately 5--10 mrad. An empirical response model calibrated to these data augments Geant4 ionisation information with gas-transport and readout effects, reproducing ten of twelve angular widths within approximately 20% and all spatial-residual widths within approximately 12%. Application without re-tuning to an independent 5 mm-drift measurement shows larger angular discrepancies. Our response model therefore provides input to feasibility studies of future compact tracking detectors.

items.title: Multiscale Renormalization of Weighted Networks
items.summary: Recent progress in network renormalization has identified various ways to transform network representations consistently across resolution levels. In particular, the renormalization flow describing how random graph models transform under node aggregation has identified a fixed point corresponding to an aggregation-invariant model that preserves the form of the connection probability across arbitrary scales. While this probabilistic multiscale approach has successfully been used to model real-world networks, construct latent-space node embeddings, and reconstruct finer-grained versions of aggregate network data in a principled resolution-invariant way, it has so far been restricted to binary graphs. Here we reformulate multiscale network renormalization for weighted random graphs. Via a generating-function approach, we identify a weighted multiscale model whose full probability law, encoding both link creation and weight assignment, has an invariant compound-Poisson form under arbitrary node aggregation. The renormalization rules that transform parameters across aggregation levels allow the ensemble to be calibrated at one level and applied at another, enabling consistent modeling and reconstruction of weighted networks across arbitrary scales.

items.title: Who Moved My $Z$ Boson? Revealing Resonance Features Inside a Neural Network
items.summary: Methods used in mechanistic interpretability have revealed human-aligned concepts inside language and image models. In this paper, we search for physics concepts inside a neural a generative collider physics model trained on real LHC data (ShellFlow). We discover features inside ShellFlow that represent resonances, such as the $Z$, $J/ψ$, and $Υ$. The network was never told which muons come from a resonance, it was only trained to generate the kinematics of the final-state particles. We use these features to alter aspects of the $Z$ boson: we change its mass between $\sim80$ and $105$ GeV, and removing such a feature from the neural network produces a broader $Z$ peak. In both cases the rest of the invariant mass spectrum remains mostly unchanged. The feature was built from the gradients of the neural network, and its selectivity was built using pattern recognition methods. A generative particle physics model trained on unlabeled data can be modified internally to change a physical quantity.

items.title: Multiscale Reconstruction of Weighted Networks from Coarse-Grained Data
items.summary: Network reconstruction from partial information is usually performed at the same resolution level at which constraints are observable. This becomes problematic when only coarse-grained information is available, while the relevant process occurs at a finer scale. Here we employ the multiscale model of weighted networks introduced in a companion paper and turn it into a probabilistic framework for reconstructing weighted networks across arbitrary aggregation levels. The model is built to preserve its functional form under coarse-graining, so that global parameters calibrated on an observable aggregate layer can be transferred to finer layers without refitting. We test the method on two empirical systems with different aggregation mechanisms. In the International Trade Network, countries are aggregated into geographic macro-regions and the observed coarse-grained layer is used to infer the underlying country-level network. In the Dutch production network, sectoral flows are reconstructed across the hierarchical industrial classification, using coarser sectoral layers to infer finer ones. In both geographical and sectoral settings, we benchmark our genuinely multiscale reconstruction method against a state-of-the-art weighted reconstruction model calibrated directly at the target resolution, and therefore using additional information available at the same (finer) scale at which performance is evaluated. Despite this informational disadvantage, our method recovers the fine-scale binary structure with high accuracy, improving precision, specificity, accuracy and maximum degree-error diagnostics, while remaining nearly equivalent in sensitivity.

items.title: Chiral Temporal Structures in Molecular Rotational Dynamics
items.summary: We introduce chiral rotational wavepackets: coherent superpositions of a few low-lying rotational states of a molecule for which the expectation value of a molecular axis traces a three-dimensional chiral trajectory in the laboratory frame. The handedness is a dynamical property of the quantum state rather than of the equilibrium structure, and we show that it can be imprinted on linear rotors as well as on spherical and symmetric tops. We derive the action of space inversion, time reversal, and their product on such wavepackets in the Wigner $D^J_{MK}$ basis, and define the rotational enantiomers of a given wavepacket. To quantify their handedness we introduce two derivative-based pseudoscalar measures: a geometrical measure built from the curvature and torsion of the trajectory, which is even under time reversal, and a dynamical measure, which is odd under time reversal. The latter is shown to be proportional to the geodesic curvature of the trajectory projected onto the unit sphere, which links it, via the Gauss--Bonnet theorem, to the solid angle enclosed by the projected trajectory and to the parallel-transport holonomy of a molecule-fixed vector. Finally we show that a nonzero geometrical measure is a sufficient condition for the wavepacket to exhibit true chirality through its orientation trajectory in the sense of Barron.

items.title: A Volume of Fluid Immersed Boundary Method for Industrial Polymer Mixing
items.summary: Free-surface numerical simulation of polymer mixing processes requires handling rotating solid boundaries of complex shapes as well as kinematic viscosity ratios between polymer melt and air up to $10^8$. We present a finite volume method that couples a Volume of Fluid (VOF) interface-capturing scheme with a non-conforming immersed boundary (IB) method, so that moving screws are represented on a fixed mesh without remeshing. In standard segregated VOF solvers, part of the viscous stress is treated explicitly, which can lead to instabilities and severe time-step restrictions at such viscosity ratios. To address this limitation, we integrate into the VOF-IB framework a block-coupled (BC) scheme in which the full viscous stress, including its transposed-gradient part, is treated implicitly. The method is implemented in the finite volume library OpenFOAM. On a three-dimensional injection-molding test case with a generalized Newtonian melt, segregated solvers either diverge or produce spurious air-phase velocities at the time steps allowed by the block-coupled solver, which instead yields a physical solution and reduces the computing time by a factor of about 2.7 with respect to the fastest segregated run that remains physical. On the finer grid, the IB solution agrees with the conforming-mesh solution within 2% in velocity and 0.5% in pressure drop. The BC-VOF-IB solver is then applied to single- and twin-screw extruders under fully and partially filled conditions, capturing the filling dynamics and the resulting pressure build-up along the screw, demonstrating the applicability of the method to industrial geometries. The current formulation is isothermal; its extension to non-isothermal flows, required for quantitative prediction of melt temperature and viscous heating, is the subject of ongoing work.

items.title: Efficient calculation of the full Laguerre-Gaussian spectrum of entangled biphotons
items.summary: The spatial biphoton state generated by spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) enables applications in high-dimensional quantum information processing and is often described in Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) modes. However, calculating the full LG spectrum for arbitrary radial and orbital angular momentum (OAM) indices requires computationally demanding multidimensional integrations. We present a generating-function approach that analytically performs the four-dimensional transverse spatial integral without approximating the phase-matching function. The source geometry can be completely described by a few dimensionless parameters, which reduce to two parameters for wave-vector-degenerate photons with equal waists. Our derived expressions for the full LG spectrum allow for computationally efficient and numerically stable evaluation at high mode orders, addressing a crucial obstacle in previous works. To illustrate our approach, we compare OAM spectra obtained by projection onto the lowest radial order and by radially insensitive detection, and investigate how high-dimensional maximal entanglement can be approached by tuning source parameters. Our results provide a new analytical tool for efficiently characterizing and engineering high-dimensional spatial entanglement in SPDC.

items.title: Flux-induced condensation in a radial geometry
items.summary: Stirring and shear usually suppress phase separation, but transport through a boundary can induce it. We study a binary mixture that is stable everywhere at rest and fills a two-dimensional annulus. The inner boundary is semipermeable and exchanges material with a permeate held at a fixed chemical potential, so that a steady flux of one component crosses the annulus. Although this driven system carries a steady current and produces entropy, within Model B dynamics its steady state is an equilibrium profile in an effective external field that is logarithmic in the distance from the center. Its strength is not imposed from outside but set by the permeate and the permeability of the boundary. Above a threshold driving flux, a condensed annulus forms around the inner boundary. It is bounded by a stationary front whose radius depends exponentially on the ratio of the bulk driving force to the flux. The front is pinned by the effective field and does not coarsen, and the threshold flux decreases only as the inverse logarithm of the system size. The driving flux shifts the phase lines but leaves the critical temperature unchanged. Interfacial tension gives rise to a critical nucleus and to a fold, at which the condensed state ceases to exist, with a threshold that we obtain in closed form. Numerical solutions confirm these predictions and reveal a hysteresis loop bounded by two saddle-node bifurcations. By symmetry, the theory also describes cavitation around a sink.

items.title: Triplet adiabatic potential energy surfaces for the O($^3$P) + C$_2$(X$^1Σ_g^+$, a$^3Π_u$) reaction and quasiclassical trajectory dynamics
items.summary: We present three global adiabatic potential energy surfaces (PESs) for the O($^3$P) + C$_2$(X $^1Σ_g^+$, a $^3Π_u$) to CO(X$^1Σ^+$) + C($^3$P) reaction, computed at the icMRCI+Q/aug-cc-pVTZ level. This reaction is relevant to combustion chemistry, atmospheric processes, and astrochemistry. Since the energy difference between the $^1Σ_g^+$ and $^3Π_u$ states of C$_2$ is smaller than the zero-point energy, both states mix upon interaction with the approaching O atom. Consequently, the PESs exhibit a double-well topography in the reactant valley. Beyond this feature, the three PESs display markedly different topographies. The 1 $^3A''$ PES features a deep minimum 7.16 eV below the O + C$_2$ entrance channel. In contrast, the 2 $^3A''$ and 1 $^3A'$ surfaces possess shallower collinear wells ($\approx$ 5.7 eV) and strong angular anisotropy arising from avoided crossings with higher-lying triplet states. The analytical fits reproduce the \textit{ab initio} data with root-mean-square (RMS) deviations of 0.022--0.028 eV over an energy interval exceeding 13 eV. Quasiclassical trajectory (QCT) calculations reveal higher reactivity on the barrierless $1\,^3A''$ surface compared to the $2\,^3A''$ PES, where an angle-dependent entrance barrier reduces the cross sections. Furthermore, cross sections for reactions initiated from C$_2$(X $^1Σ_g^+$) and C$_2$(a $^3Π_u$) are remarkably similar for the three PESs, regardless of the initial rovibrational state.

items.title: Resonant filling for long-pulse operation of EuXFEL using iterative learning based feed forward
items.summary: A future operation scenario of the European XFEL (EuXFEL) is long-pulse (LP) mode, where the 800 superconducting radio frequency (SRF) cavities of the linac are energized with RF pulse lengths of up to 500ms. Compared to the current, short-pulse (SP) mode with less than 2ms, the dominant mechanical eigenmodes of the cavities at a few hundred Hertz pose a significant control challenge, as the RF pulse extends beyond a multiple of their periods. To improve energy efficiency of LP operation, cavities are operated at bandwidths in the range of tens of Hertz, a factor of 10 narrower than in SP. Due to peak power limitation of the proposed high power amplifiers, even the fill time surpasses mechanical mode periods. This paper presents experimental evaluation of two feed forward adaptation approaches to facilitate resonant-filling despite mechanical mode transients: In a single-cavity regulation setup, the RF drive phase is adjusted to match the Lorentz force detuning induced cavity phase shift. In vector-sum RF regulation systems, the incident phase cannot be adjusted to each cavity individually, so the concept is inverted by adapting mechanical cavity tuner drives to match each individual cavity resonance trajectory with a fixed common RF drive phase.

items.title: Theory of magneto-electrokinetics in unidirectional electrolyte flow: Hydrodynamic potential and Hall effect
items.summary: We develop a theoretical framework for magneto-electrokinetic transport in dilute electrolytes under unidirectional flow and streaming current conditions. Unlike standard magnetohydrodynamics in liquid metals, where charge carriers are electrons and conductivity is typically uniform, electrolytes exhibit spatially varying ion densities and additional forces such as osmotic pressure. In steady state, the coupled Navier--Stokes, Nernst--Planck, and Poisson equations become analytically tractable. We derive a Boltzmann-like expression for ion distributions that incorporates both the electrostatic potential and a novel hydrodynamic potential arising from the magnetic field. This potential depends explicitly on the flow profile and is not screened close to the bounding walls. Applying the theory to Poiseuille flow, we derive expressions for the induced Hall potential and demonstrate its near-linear dependence on flow velocity and magnetic field strength, while remaining largely independent of salt concentration. To validate this one-dimensional framework, we analyze the two-dimensional spatial transients near the channel entrance. We demonstrate a separation of length scales: the Hall electric field and space charge adjust to the magnetic field almost instantaneously, whereas the macroscopic salt concentration wake develops over a much longer Graetz length dictated by the Péclet number. We also examine a similar flow with counterions only and no added salt, determining the resulting potential and ion distributions. This work offers new theoretical tools for understanding ion transport in microfluidic and electrochemical systems.

items.title: Role of Metastable Dicationic Intermediates in the Breakup of CH$_4^{2+}$
items.summary: We investigate the fragmentation dynamics of methane dication (CH$_4^{2+}$) produced in collisions with 50-MeV C$^{6+}$ ions using the COLTRIMS technique. The method provides complete three-dimensional momentum vectors of the charged fragments, enabling full kinematic reconstruction of the fragmentation process. The dynamics are analyzed using Dalitz plots, Newton diagrams, and the native-frame method to distinguish between concerted and sequential dissociation mechanisms. The data indicate the presence of sequential fragmentation pathways for the CH$_4^{2+}$ $\rightarrow$ CH$_2^+$ + H$^+$ + H, CH$_4^{2+}$ $\rightarrow$ CH$^+$ + H$^+$ + 2H, and CH$_4^{2+}$ $\rightarrow$ C$^+$ + H$^+$ + 3H channels, consistent with dissociation via short-lived dicationic intermediates CH$_3^{2+}$, CH$_2^{2+}$, and CH$^{2+}$, respectively. From the Newton-diagram momentum distributions, we estimate half-rotational periods of approximately 180~fs, 71~fs, and 44~fs for the $\mathrm{CH_3^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{CH_2^{2+}}$, and $\mathrm{CH^{2+}}$ intermediates, respectively, providing characteristic lower-limit timescales for their survival prior to fragmentation. The experimental observations are further supported by comparisons with calculated potential-energy curves.

items.title: Direct visualization of charge dynamics by Pockels imaging in optoelectronics
items.summary: Understanding charge dynamics in optoelectronic devices is essential because it governs carrier transport, signal evolution, and device performance. Yet, experimental access to the spatiotemporal evolution of charge remains limited. Here, we introduce Carrier Dynamics by Pockels Imaging (CDPI), a sensitive, quantitative, and non-invasive pump-probe technique based on the linear electro-optic (Pockels) effect. CDPI images the electric-field wave associated with traveling photogenerated carriers and reveals the evolution of charge clouds in space and time. This provides direct access to fundamental transport processes, including drift, diffusion, carrier-carrier interactions, trapping, and detrapping. Furthermore, the internal conduction- and displacement-current profiles are obtained from the electric-field dynamics and shown to be consistent with the externally measured current transients. Demonstrated in CdTe radiation detectors with micrometre-scale spatial resolution and nanosecond temporal resolution, CDPI is applicable to materials exhibiting a measurable Pockels effect, including electro-optic semiconductors, oxides, halide perovskites, organic materials, and emerging low-dimensional systems, providing a platform to investigate charge transport across optoelectronics.

items.title: The long-term divergence exponent and the temporal structure of step-to-step perturbations: a simulation study in two passive walking models
items.summary: Purpose. Divergence exponents are used to assess the local dynamic stability of gait. Human experiments have related the long-term exponent ($λ_L$) to the complexity of gait fluctuations. Model studies used perturbations without controlled temporal structure. The question was whether $λ_L$ responds to the temporal structure of perturbations in walkers without neuromuscular control. Methods. Two passive walkers, M1 (pilot) and M2 (exploratory), received step-to-step perturbations of five amplitudes ($σ$) and nine temporal structures (ARFIMA parameter $d$), and human stride series of free and metronome walking. Results. At constant amplitude, $λ_L$ increased with $d$ in both models. It was higher with free series than with metronome series or with surrogates. It did not follow $σ$ in M1 and followed $σ$ in M2. Its double dissociation from the short-term exponent was supported in M1 only. In a descriptive analysis, the condition means of $λ_L$ correlated with the scaling exponent of the step durations ($r = 0.980$ in M1 and 0.906 in M2). Conclusion. In two passive walkers with fixed mechanics, $λ_L$ followed the temporal structure of the perturbations; its specificity depended on the model. This response supports the name attractor complexity index (ACI), proposed for $λ_L$ from human experiments.

items.title: DUV (257 nm) LIDT of Anti-Reflective Coatings
items.summary: Laser-induced damage threshold in the deep ultraviolet (DUV) was used to perform tests on AR coated windows intended for industrial processes. The 257 nm wavelength was generated from Yb:YAG fundamental (1030 nm) and the long-term LIDT stability (up to 100000 shots) was selected as representative for minimal industrial qualification. Selected setup for the fourth harmonics generation consists of two stages, generation of second harmonic and subsequently the fourth harmonic with 13,4% conversation efficiency. In both 1-on-1 and S-on-1 experiments, the optics coated with Al2O3/SiO2 by ion beam sputtering technique demonstrated the highest LIDT value of 0.73 and 0.5 J/cm2 respectively. Various damage morphologies, color centers, ballistic damage, delamination, and blistering were observed across the samples with respect to the 1-on-1 and S-on-1.

items.title: Entropy: the Route from the Gaussian Field to the Statistical Mechanics of the Thermal Radiation
items.summary: Maximum Entropy or canonical typicality applied to the electromagnetic field can provide starting points for arriving at the Bose distribution of the photon numbers of thermal radiation, but they rely on statistical postulates whose experimental testability is controversial. Here we start from the experimentally verifiable assumption of Gaussianity of the electromagnetic field. We analyze the field by projecting it onto orthonormal time-frequency basis functions with unitary bandwidth duration product that represent field's orthogonal time-frequency modes. Through the Glauber-Surashdan representation, we see that the joint density operator of the modes in the photon number basis factorize into diagonal density operators with geometric coefficients of individual modes, while the mean photon occupations of the modes remains still unknown. Imposing Clausius' relation on the entropy rates and energy rates of the independent modes we get Bose's mean photon occupancy. Thus, our main claim is that for the first time Bose statistics is obtained under explicit, experimentally verifiable statistical assumptions, without any assumption that is not experimentally verifiable. From the mean occupation numbers, the Boltzmann distribution of the energy of matter particles of the material that generates/absorbes the radiation is then derived by retracing in the backward direction the Einstein-Feynman detailed balance.

items.title: Dual Action of Electrolyte Additives in High-Voltage Li-Ion Cells
items.summary: Electrolyte additives have outsized effects on cell performance, but determining their mechanism of action can be difficult. Here, we evaluate whether simple electrochemical tests can reveal which electrode (cathode, anode or both) is targeted by specific additives. Our experiments quantified the rates of reductive and oxidative side-reactions in NMC532 vs. graphite cells containing 12 different electrolyte formulations. We found that gains in interphasial stability were highly correlated, with successful additives decreasing both types of side-reactions by similar magnitude. This dual action could be indicative of the role of crosstalk on cell degradation, as soluble species formed on one electrode can decompose at the other end of the cell. Although electrochemical tests are insufficient for understanding mechanisms of improvement, they can reveal interesting effects that complement other characterization tools.

items.title: Higher-Order Functional Networks from Event Time Series
items.summary: Inferring relations among the units of a complex system from their activity is a fundamental problem across many fields. Here, we introduce a method to identify functional dependencies of arbitrary order from multivariate event time series. The method maps the data onto a symbolic sequence, and uses a Bayesian framework to extract statistically significant motifs of symbols. These motifs define the hyperedges of a hypergraph, providing a compact representation of higher-order functional dependencies in their original data and enabling their analysis with network-based tools. Applications to neural and social systems reveal nontrivial higher-order dependencies associated with collective brain activity and social behaviour. Our framework thus provides a general approach for uncovering higher-order functional organization directly from event data.

items.title: Hierarchical Reconstruction of Time-arrow from Multi-time Correlations
items.summary: The entropy production rate (EPR), a key measure of thermodynamic irreversibility in thermodynamics of small systems, is difficult to determine directly in experiments, motivating lower-bound-based estimation from observations. However, a systematic framework for organizing increasing amounts of the irreversibility information in experimental state observables into progressively tighter bounds remains lacking. Here, we show that multi-time correlations of a class of state observations naturally encode this information to provide a hierarchy. By defining a reconstruction operation as a combination of correlations, we obtain a sequence of lower bounds on the EPR. Correlations of higher order capture the thermodynamic information at greater temporal depth, thereby capturing more irreversibility and yielding tighter bounds. Under ideal conditions, this hierarchy converges to the full EPR in the limit of infinitely dense observations over a finite time window.

items.title: A Paired Monte Carlo Intensity-Ratio Method for Incorporating Detector Resolution in Amplitude Analysis
items.summary: Finite detector resolution can bias resonance parameters and fit fractions extracted from amplitude analyses. We present the paired Monte Carlo intensity-ratio method for incorporating resolution effects into amplitude analysis. The method uses ratios of reference intensities evaluated at paired truth-level and reconstructed kinematics to reweight the Monte Carlo normalization and approximately account for detector resolution. A resampling study of simulated $D^+\to K^+π^+π^-π^0$ decays shows that the method substantially reduces resolution-induced shifts in fitted resonance widths. Likelihood evaluation uses intensity calculations and normalization sums, avoiding a response convolution at each data event.

items.title: Transition Dynamics Matter: Hidden Markov Scoring of Epileptogenic Channels in SEEG
items.summary: Stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) represents the most effective technique for the detection of the Epileptogenic Zone (EZ) in drug-resistant epilepsy. This procedure produces a multi-dimensional signal with hundreds of components, named channels, each associated with a different brain location. In this work, we propose a joint Hidden Markov Model (HMM), in which each SEEG channel is described by a latent Markov chain, with states shared across the network and channel-specific transition probabilities. Accordingly, we develop a detection algorithm that identifies the channels belonging to the EZ by quantifying, through the Kullback-Leibler divergence, the difference between their transition probabilities in the inter-ictal period and at seizure onset. We evaluate our framework in SEEG recordings from 30 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy and compare it with a benchmark that operates in the same observation space but does not consider a latent-state structure. Compared against medically validated EZ definitions, our study shows that modeling channel-specific temporal transitions can improve EZ localization and offer a data-driven framework to investigate the latent dynamics underlying seizures.

items.title: On the Coupled Cluster Doubles Truncation Variety of Four Electrons
items.summary: We extend recent algebro-geometric results for coupled cluster theory of quantum many-body systems to the truncation varieties arising from the doubles approximation (CCD), focusing on the first genuinely nonlinear doubles regime of four electrons. Since this doubles truncation variety does not coincide with previously studied varieties, we initiate a systematic investigation of its basic algebro-geometric invariants. We show that for $4$ electrons in $n \geq 13$ orbitals, the CCD truncation variety is not a complete intersection, and we present numerical and symbolic evidence that for the remaining cases it is a complete intersection defined by $\binom{n-4}{4}$ quadrics. Using representation-theoretic arguments, we uncover a Pfaffian structure governing the quadratic relations that define the truncation variety for any $n$, and show that an exact tensor product factorization holds in the distinguished limit of disconnected doubles. We connect these structural results to the computation of the beryllium insertion into molecular hydrogen ({Be$\cdots$H$_2$ $\to$ H--Be--H}), a small but computationally challenging bond formation process where multiconfigurational effects become pronounced.

items.title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning for Shear Wave Speed Estimation in MR Elastography
items.summary: Objective: Magnetic Resonance Elastography (MRE) is a non-invasive imaging technique for mapping biomechanical properties of in vivo tissue, including shear wave speed (SWS), but involves intrinsically slow data acquisition and an ill-posed wave inversion. Instead of relying on handcrafted image priors, we propose a data-driven approach jointly combining image reconstruction and MRE inversion for robust SWS estimation from undersampled k-space data. Methods: Our physics-informed reconstruction framework comprises two blocks: a model-based neural network (NN)-regularized reconstruction module and a phase-gradient inversion (k-MDEV) calculating SWS from the reconstructed images. Concatenating both blocks yields an end-to-end trainable method to estimate SWS directly from measured k-space data. We evaluated the method on retrospectively highly undersampled brain MRE data and compared it to a total variation (TV) minimization-based approach. We assessed the impact of end-to-end training (qualitative images and SWS maps as targets) versus pre-training (qualitative images as targets) and applied the method also to in vivo data. Results: Our approach significantly reduces NRMSE by 30% compared to TV. End-to-end training improves SWS estimation over separate image reconstruction and SWS calculation. Conclusion: Accurate SWS quantification is possible at acceleration factors up to 19. Our method significantly outperforms TV, highlighting the need for data-driven regularization in this challenging MR problem. Further, our approach successfully generalizes to in vivo data. Significance: We present the first end-to-end trainable MRE reconstruction method for estimating SWS maps directly from k-space. NN-based reconstruction can enable rapid stiffness mapping for dynamic studies, functional imaging, and real-time clinical feedback.

items.title: High-Speed Widefield Hyperspectral Imaging
items.summary: Fourier-transform hyperspectral imaging is an emerging technology that combines widefield acquisition with flexible spectral resolution. Yet, it typically requires the acquisition of dense sequences of full-field interferograms during optical-path scanning, which ultimately reduces the final throughput. To circumvent this limitation, this manuscript introduces an event-based Fourier-transform hyperspectral microscopy technique that exploits the coupling of a neuromorphic event camera with a common-path birefringent interferometer operated under continuous scanning. Specifically, two complementary acquisition strategies are investigated, one with steady broadband illumination where the event stream corresponds to a derivative-like interferogram, and another with a temporal modulation of a broadband LED, which produces an intensity-like event response. Both approaches are able to retrieve the principal spectral profiles of photographic filters, showing a good qualitative match with both frame-based and spectrometer references. Compared against the typical 15-minute acquisition time for step-scan reference configuration, both methods represent a speedup larger than 3 orders of magnitude, entering real-time acquisition speeds: the derivative-based method acquires the useful interferometric range in approximately 200 ms, corresponding to an effective rate of approximately 5 hyperspectral cubes per second, whereas the modulation-assisted method achieves an experimentally measured spectral resolution of 17.9 nm at an effective acquisition rate of 2.5 datacubes per second. Finally, reflection-mode imaging and motion-compensated reconstruction of moving particles further demonstrate spatially resolved spectral recovery beyond static transmission measurements, establishing the solution as a promising technology for continuous, wide-field hyperspectral imaging.

items.title: Approximate Adjoint Models for Memory and Compute-Efficient Online Learning of Hybrid Models
items.summary: Differentiable programming enables online calibration of numerical models by minimizing errors accumulated along simulated trajectories. This includes estimating physical parameters and training neural sub-models in hybrid configurations. Gradients are typically computed using adjoint methods, or backpropagation through time (BPTT), whose computational and memory costs grow with the length of the training window. This limits the duration and resolution of hybrid-model training, a major bottleneck for realistic geophysical applications. Approaches like truncated BPTT reduces memory use by discarding sensitivities across truncation boundaries, introducing gradient bias and neglecting long-range dependencies. We propose a class of gradient approximation methods that preserve the adjoint recurrence over the full trajectory while approximating only the pullback operators within it. Exact pullbacks are computed by automatic differentiation at sparse anchor states only. Between anchors, sensitivities propagate either through the identity (Zero-order) or through a reused, frozen pullback (Pullback Reuse). This approximation makes the parameter pullback constant within each chunk, allowing the gradient sum to factorize so that a single evaluation per chunk replaces one per time step. We evaluate both on three systems of increasing complexity, an incomplete Lorenz-63 model, a large-eddy closure for two-dimensional quasi-geostrophic turbulence, and bias correction in a multilayer quasi-geostrophic ocean model. Peak memory falls by up to an order of magnitude and runtime up to fourfold, with Pullback Reuse staying closest to the exact gradient direction. In all three cases, approximate gradients support hybrid-model training at comparable accuracy, showing that effective online learning does not require exact gradients.

items.title: Xaurora: Generative Weather Forecasting with Denoising Stochastic Interpolants from a Foundation Model Prior
items.summary: Deep learning has revolutionised weather forecasting in recent years, especially through atmospheric foundation models, which offer competitive skill for a fraction of the computational costs of classic physics-based models. However, most existing foundation models are deterministic, limiting the generation of large ensembles for accurate uncertainty quantification, extreme weather risk assessment, and long-range weather forecasting. Furthermore, these models incur a large, often prohibitive, computational overhead to train from scratch. To address these shortcomings, we turn a pretrained deterministic prior model, namely the Aurora foundation model, into a generative ensemble-prediction model. To that end, we introduce a novel generative method, Denoising Stochastic Interpolants, combined with a replay buffer for Stochastic Differential Equation (SDE) rollout, enabling probabilistic training of SDE trajectories. Our stochastic foundation model, Xaurora, is finetuned from the small Aurora version, yet it approaches the state-of-the-art on global ensemble metrics and is competitive with the large version of Aurora. Our method is parameter and sample efficient, and generates skilful 15-day forecasts in 7 minutes. Our results demonstrate that deterministic foundation models can be efficiently extended into even stronger stochastic models.

items.title: Finite-Key Analysis for Multiple-Antenna Quantum Key Distribution with Continuous Variables
items.summary: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) techniques, known for their use in wireless communications, can also find applications in quantum communications systems. This is, for instance, relevant to satellite-based quantum communications when atmospheric turbulence and the time-varying nature of the channel can make their implementation difficult. Here, we study the application of MIMO techniques to continuous-variable (CV) quantum key distribution (QKD) in the realistic setting where a finite number of signals are exchanged. We show how data collected during the brief overpass time of low-earth-orbit satellites over ground stations can be processed to estimate MIMO channel parameters, extract a secret key, and quantify the key generation rate. For $2\times 2$ MIMO settings with Gaussian encoding and heterodyne detection, our finite-key analysis indicates that MIMO CV-QKD could outperform both multiplexed (with a nominal 3~dB improvement) and single-mode (with a nominal 6~dB nominal improvement) scenarios. Furthermore, we conjecture that the ultimate enhancement of a multiple-antenna CV-QKD system can be characterized by the product of the number of its inputs and outputs.

items.title: Influence of an oxide cap on the combustion of aluminum particles using boundary-layer resolved simulations
items.summary: A distinctive feature of burning aluminum particles is the condensation of the primary combustion product, alumina, forming an oxide cap that covers part of the aluminum particle and alters the local combustion characteristics. This study systematically investigates the effects of an oxide cap on the combustion characteristics and interfacial processes of aluminum particles, using boundary-layer resolved simulations, considering variations in cap size, cap position relative to the flow direction, and the particle Reynolds number, $\mathrm{Re_p}$. The oxide cap modifies both the interfacial transfer and the surrounding combustion characteristics. Front caps enhance local evaporation near the junction between the cap and the aluminum body, whereas heat absorption by rear caps contributes to lower reaction temperatures. Variations in integrated heat release generally follow those in the evaporation rate. Based on the simulation results, the Lagrangian modeling framework was first revised for spherical particles. The film state is approximated using a 0.55-rule applied to temperature, species mass fractions, and pressure, from which the remaining thermophysical properties are derived. A simplified composition scheme enables film-state viscosity and fuel diffusivity to be pre-calculated as functions of temperature. Optimized Whitaker and Schiller-Naumann correlations were developed for the mass evaporation rate and drag force coefficient, respectively, showing good agreement with the simulation results. The framework was further extended to doublet particles with oxide caps. Accounting for the exposed aluminum area provides good evaporation predictions for rear caps, while front caps require a correction to the surface-averaged evaporation mass flux, particularly at high $\mathrm{Re_p}$.

items.title: SlotFlow-GB: A Neural Framework for Trans-Dimensional Inference of Overlapping Galactic Binaries
items.summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe the millihertz gravitational-wave sky, including millions of long-lived Galactic binaries (GBs), tens of thousands of which are expected to be individually resolvable throughout the mission's lifetime. Extracting these sources requires jointly determining their number and physical parameters from strongly overlapping signals, posing a computationally demanding trans-dimensional inference problem. We introduce SlotFlow-GB, a neural framework that constructs a learned approximation to the trans-dimensional posterior, producing a probability distribution over source multiplicity and parameter densities for individual binaries in a single evaluation, without requiring their number to be specified in advance. We demonstrate this framework using year-long LISA simulations containing up to ten binaries within a 2 $μ$Hz frequency interval, focusing on a high-SNR regime in which source overlap, rather than individual-source detectability, is the primary challenge. The inferred source count differs from the true count by at most one in 94% of cases, while the model identifies individual binaries even when their signals overlap strongly in frequency. A complete evaluation, including parameter sampling, takes just 41 ms per band on one NVIDIA GH200 GPU, or 530 ms on eight laptop CPU threads. We further demonstrate that these distributions can be used to initialize subsequent likelihood-based inference, connecting fast amortized predictions with joint parameter estimation.

items.title: Swimming formula in a linearly viscous fluid with anisotropic and odd viscosity tensors at low Reynolds number
items.summary: We theoretically investigate the low-Reynolds-number hydrodynamics of a microswimmer in a linearly viscous fluid. The fluid is characterized by a viscosity tensor containing both even and odd components, and can therefore exhibit anisotropic and chiral properties absent in an isotropic Newtonian fluid. By employing the generalized Lorentz reciprocal theorem, we establish the Onsager-Casimir reciprocity for the resistance tensors of an arbitrarily shaped rigid body. We then derive a swimming formula that linearly relates the swimming velocities to the prescribed surface velocity of a microswimmer and imposed background flows. As a showcase application of the derived swimming formula, we prove that the scallop theorem holds in this class of linearly viscous fluids. Furthermore, we investigate the equations of motion for a spherical swimmer in a fluid with odd viscosity, as a representative example of the generalized linear constitutive framework. In particular, we reveal that sufficiently strong shear flows destabilize the bimodal chirotactic alignment of a microswimmer. Our results highlight how intrinsic fluid chirality and anisotropy fundamentally alter the orientational dynamics and transport phenomena of microswimmers.

items.title: Bifurcation analysis of particulate Rayleigh-Benard convection
items.summary: Particles carried through a convecting fluid layer exchange momentum and heat with the fluid, and so change not only where convection starts but also how it saturates. We study this coupling in the particulate Rayleigh-Benard system, in which a dilute stream of thermally inertial particles is injected at one wall and removed at the other. An Eulerian two-fluid model retaining drag, pressure-gradient, added-mass, and buoyancy forces and interphase heat exchange describes heavy particles and bubbles through a single density parameter beta. After reproducing the linear stability results of Raza et al. (2025a), we use a multiple-scale expansion and a Fredholm solvability condition to compute the first Landau coefficient a1 near onset. At low and moderate particle loading, the bifurcation is supercritical for every density ratio considered, extending the conclusion of Srinivas and Tomar (2025) for very heavy particles. At higher flux, however, Re(a1) changes sign, and the onset becomes subcritical over a broad band of density ratios, from moderately heavy particles injected below their terminal speed to most light particles. In the plane of density ratio and injection velocity, this band is bounded by lines of tricritical points. Splitting a1 by the balance equation shows that its sign is set almost entirely by the fluid energy equation, while the direct nonlinear terms of the particle equations are five to six orders of magnitude smaller. The particles thus change the nature of the bifurcation indirectly, through the base state and the linear mode they help to shape, rather than through their own nonlinear dynamics.

items.title: Three-mode chimera-like states in a minimal network of active camphor ribbons
items.summary: Chimera states are a remarkable manifestation of symmetry breaking, wherein identical units spontaneously split into coherent and incoherent groups. The term "chimera" itself is inspired by the mythological creature having parts of different animals, reflecting the coexistence of distinct dynamical behaviors within a single system. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the existence of a three-mode chimera-like state in a system of four identical camphor-infused elliptical rotors, each pivoted at a corner of a square base. When placed on a water surface, the rotors self-propel and rotate due to Marangoni-driven flows. Chemical coupling mediated through the shared water interface gives rise to three distinct collective dynamical states, namely a synchronized one, an antisynchronized one and an incoherent one. Our results validate recent theoretical work about three-domain chimeras in reaction-diffusion models, providing new insights into nonlinear dynamics and suggesting that this new type of chimera may be observed in a broad class of physical systems.

items.title: The Ionospheric Cut-off as a Potential Radio Technosignature
items.summary: Radio emission generated on a planetary surface must cross the planet's ionosphere before escaping into space: below the local plasma frequency it is reflected back towards the surface. We investigate this process for broadband radio technosignatures (BRaTs) using a Chapman-layer description of photoionised atmospheres. The plasma frequency depends only weakly on stellar XUV irradiation, scaling as $Q_{\infty}^{1/4}$, implying turnover frequencies of 5-40 MHz for most terrestrial habitable-zone planets, potentially rising towards 100 MHz in extreme environments. The basic signature is simple: the continuum of a surface-origin BRaT should be strongly suppressed below a characteristic frequency that can be estimated from the XUV output of the host star, at every orbital phase and for any viewing geometry. Oblique propagation, magnetic fields, and collisional absorption broaden the cut-off into a smooth escape function, $f_{\mathrm{esc}}(ν,φ)$, where $φ$ is the orbital phase. Because the day-night ionisation pattern is anchored to the substellar point rather than to the rotating surface, disc integration adds a second, more discriminating signature: the half-escape frequency $ν_{1/2}$ varies predictably (by about 40-50 per cent over the orbit, depending on the angular emission pattern of the leakage) and remains locked to the orbital ephemeris. Finite atmospheric response times introduce modest phase lags but preserve the modulation. A low-frequency turnover alone is not unique to technology, but one that varies periodically with the orbital period would be difficult to reproduce through known astrophysical processes. Although observationally challenging, the ionospheric cut-off is a potential technosignature diagnostic and a novel probe of exoplanet ionospheres.

items.title: The final stages of a Chapman-Jouguet detonation: support by its own products
items.summary: A planar Chapman-Jouguet detonation that runs out of fuel must become a shock. We show that, when the chemical energy decreases in the direction of propagation, the wave does not pass through the local Chapman-Jouguet states. The products of the richer mixture are at a higher pressure than the local Chapman-Jouguet state, so the wave is overdriven, it loses its sonic point, and forward characteristics carry the state of the rich products to the shock. The rarefaction behind the wave removes this support only if the distance travelled since initiation is small compared with the thickness of the fuel gradient, which is rarely the case. The wave speed instead approaches an envelope given by a Riemann problem between the rich products and the local mixture, ending at the Mach number of the shock transmitted into inert gas. For strong detonations this Mach number tends to a fraction $C$ of the Chapman-Jouguet value, with $0.621<C<0.625$ for every ratio of specific heats. The mechanism is purely gas-dynamic. Shock-fitted computations with a two-step chain-branching mechanism, for gradients 1 to 1000 induction lengths thick, confirm that no sonic point forms and that the induction zone never decouples.

items.title: Projection of global daily CO2 emissions in 2026
items.summary: Global fossil-fuel combustion and industrial-process CO2 emissions remain close to historical highs, yet the recent slowdown in growth is difficult to assess before conventional inventories become available. We project emissions for 2026 and examine daily departures during major climate and energy disruptions. We fit Prophet models to the latest five years of Carbon Monitor activity estimates for 47 region-sector series. We use these models to project daily emissions for October-December and combine them with activity estimates through September. Global emissions are estimated at 38.0 Gt CO2 in 2026, 34.1 Mt CO2 (-0.1%) below 2025. The hindcast-adjusted range for the annual change is -0.9% to +0.7%. Five September-cutoff hindcasts show lower mean daily errors and larger mean absolute annual biases for Prophet than for a seasonal-naive benchmark. Regional increases total 0.331 Gt and decreases total 0.365 Gt, so 95.1% of the 0.696 Gt gross movement cancels in the global sum. China contributes the largest reduction (-0.243 Gt), concentrated in industry and ground transport, whereas India contributes the largest increase (+0.222 Gt), led by power and industry. Heat-period power anomalies differ among countries and can be muted by summer averaging, while aviation and shipping show different disruption and recovery profiles. Resolving the near-zero global change reveals where reductions are concentrated and where continued growth offsets them, providing a timely basis for assessing the breadth of mitigation progress.

items.title: Doubly resonant nonlinear metasurfaces enabling NIR-to-UV upconversion for reconfigurable Fourier optical processing
