We model a financial market as an ecology of two trading-behavior types, relatively rational (R) and boundedly rational (N), whose composition evolves under replicator dynamics according to relative performance. Each type's fitness depends on the share of the other type and on frictions. When the interaction is complementary, that is, rational traders profit from the mispricing created by boundedly rational traders while the latter benefit from the liquidity and price correction supplied by the former, and when the difference in frictions is moderate, a unique interior composition exists and is globally asymptotically stable: bounded rationality persists endogenously. When the interaction is antagonistic, the same point becomes a tipping threshold between two one-type regimes. Comparative statics show that lowering the costs of disciplined trading, as algorithmic and AI-based trading does, shifts the composition toward rational trading continuously but does not eliminate bounded rationality unless the cost advantage exceeds an explicit threshold.

items.title: Mean Field Games of Optimal Trading with an SPDE Model of the Limit Order Book
items.summary: We develop a mean field game model for optimal trading in which the interaction among traders is mediated by the dynamics of the limit order book. The bid- and ask-side order densities are modelled as stochastic processes with values in infinite-dimensional function spaces that solve stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) with stochastic order submission rates and multiplicative infinite-dimensional noise. This extends an existing limit order book framework to capture the aggregate impact of the strategic traders on the order densities. Trading activity affects the order densities, which determine the market depths near the best quotes and hence the mid-price, and the mid-price in turn affects the traders' decisions. We establish the well-posedness and regularity of the resulting density-price system and use it to formulate an $N$-player optimal trading game in which the traders' market orders enter the book through their aggregate order flow. We then study the corresponding mean field game as the number of traders tends to infinity, characterize the mean field equilibrium as a fixed point of the associated consistency condition, and prove its existence and uniqueness under suitable conditions. Finally, we show that the mean field equilibrium induces an $ε_N$-Nash equilibrium for the finite-player game, with $ε_N=O(N^{-1/2})$, and provide a numerical illustration of the equilibrium dynamics.

items.title: Eliciting ESG Preferences for Reinforcement Learning-Based Portfolio Optimization
items.summary: Modern portfolio management increasingly demands a balance between traditional risk-adjusted returns and strict Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) mandates. Current Reinforcement Learning (RL) approaches typically optimize for a single ESG provider, neglecting the significant divergence in rating methodologies across the industry and the unintuitive nature of manually weighting conflicting objectives. This paper addresses these limitations by formulating ESG-aware portfolio optimization as a Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning (MORL) problem that simultaneously incorporates ratings from three distinct ESG agencies. To bridge the gap between high-dimensional algorithmic trade-offs and human decision-making, we integrate a Preference Elicitation framework using Gaussian Processes. This system enables practitioners to align the RL policy behavior with their preferences through intuitive pairwise comparisons of candidate portfolios based on their Sharpe ratios and aggregate ESG scores. We systematically evaluate our framework by employing prompt-conditioned LLMs as synthetic preference oracles under varied regional conditions and assess how the methodology adapts to heterogeneous investment behaviors and sustainability preferences. The experiments demonstrate feasibility in a controlled synthetic setting and characterize sensitivity to oracle and prompt design.

items.title: Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal Deep Learning for Prediction of Radiation-Induced Xerostomia in Head and Neck Cancer
items.summary: To develop and evaluate an uncertainty-aware multimodal learning framework for predicting radiation-induced xerostomia in patients receiving head-and-neck cancer radiotherapy. We developed a Bidirectional Attention-enhanced Diffusion Transformer (BA-DiT) that combines self-supervised multimodal representation learning with supervised Bayesian fine-tuning. The model integrates pretreatment CT images and three-dimensional dose distributions, focusing on bilateral parotid glands while incorporating surrounding anatomical and dosimetric information. During pretraining, bidirectional cross-attention integrates anatomical and dosimetric features, while a latent Diffusion Transformer learns joint representations through diffusion-based learning, feature reconstruction, and contrastive alignment. Supervised fine-tuning employs a Bayesian classifier to predict individualized xerostomia risk and quantify predictive uncertainty, with a learnable label-transition model accounting for potential toxicity label uncertainty. BA-DiT was developed using four independent cohorts (Moffitt, Emory, MSHS, and TCIA) and evaluated against baseline and ablation models. Evaluation included predictive performance, calibration, uncertainty quantification, decision curve analysis, and patient-level case studies. In independent MSHS and Emory cohorts, BA-DiT achieved AUCs of 0.83 and 0.80, respectively, outperforming baseline models. Predictive uncertainty peaked near the decision boundary, with aleatoric uncertainty being the predominant component. Uncertainty-based selective prediction generally improved net benefit among retained patients, with greater gains at lower prediction coverage. BA-DiT enables individualized xerostomia risk prediction while providing complementary uncertainty estimates, potentially supporting informed clinical decision-making and personalized toxicity management.

items.title: Load-Following Dynamics of an SMR-Powered All-Electric Ship with Battery Energy Storage
items.summary: Small modular reactors (SMRs) are being considered as compact, high-energy-density power sources for future all-electric ships. In such systems, propulsion-load variations can propagate through the electrical network, turbine-generator set, steam generator, and reactor, producing coupled nuclear, thermal, mechanical, and electrical transients. This paper presents an integrated dynamic load-following analysis of an SMR-powered all-electric ship with and without battery energy storage system (BESS) support. The model couples an integral pressurized water reactor, a once-through moving-boundary steam generator, a simplified turbine model, a synchronous generator, an AC shipboard electrical network, an asynchronous propulsion motor, and a grid-connected BESS. A propulsion-load reduction is applied through the motor torque command, and the responses of the SMR-alone and SMR+BESS configurations are compared. The results show that, without BESS support, the sudden decrease in propulsion motor power creates a temporary surplus between turbine mechanical power and electrical demand, causing a large over-frequency transient and rapid steam-cycle adjustment. With BESS support, the battery absorbs excess electrical power during the transient, reducing the frequency peak from approximately 61.1 Hz to about 60.06 Hz. The BESS also indirectly smooths the upstream steam-cycle and reactor responses, including steam flow, steam-generator pressure, feedwater flow, coolant temperature, reactivity, reactor thermal power, and steam-generator region lengths. These results demonstrate the importance of modeling nuclear-powered electric ships as coupled multi-domain systems and show that BESS integration can improve short-term load-following performance.

items.title: Unsupervised End-to-End Array Calibration for Multi-Target Integrated Sensing and Communication
items.summary: In this work, we consider end-to-end calibration of an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) base station (BS) under gain-phase and antenna displacement impairments without collecting signals from predefined positions (labeled data). We consider a BS with two impaired uniform linear arrays used for simultaneous multi-target sensing and communication with a user equipment (UE) leveraging orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing signals. The main contribution is the design of a framework that can compensate for the impairments without labeled data and considering coherent receive signals. We harness a differentiable precoder based on the maximum array response in an angular direction at the transmitter and the orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm at the sensing receiver. We propose an ISAC loss as a combination of sensing and communication losses that provides a trade-off between the two functionalities. We compare two sensing objective alternatives: (i) maximize the maximum response of the angle-delay map of the targets or (ii) minimize the norm of the residual signal at the output of the OMP algorithm after all estimated targets have been removed. The communication objective maximizes the energy of the received signal at the UE. Additionally, our framework leverages an approximation of the channel gradient that avoids the impractical knowledge of the gradient of the channel. Our results show that the proposed method performs closely to using labeled data and knowledge of the channel gradient in terms of sensing position estimation and communication symbol error rate. When comparing the two sensing losses, minimizing the norm of the OMP residual yields significantly better sensing position estimation with slightly increased complexity.

items.title: FR3-Band Capacitive-Piezoelectric Thin-Film LN Resonator for Heterogeneous Integration
items.summary: This letter presents a capacitively coupled piezoelectric lateral-field-excited bulk acoustic wave resonator (XBAR) in single-crystal lithium niobate (LN) for frequency range 3 (FR3, 7.125-24.25 GHz). We develop a platform that simultaneously maintains high electromechanical efficiency (\(k_t^2\)) and quality factor (\(Q\)) while alleviating challenges associated with parasitic galvanic interconnections and is fit for heterogeneous integration above integrated circuits. A 100 nm air gap excites the second-order symmetric Lamb wave (S2) mode in a 500 nm thick periodically poled piezoelectric film (P3F) LN from a fused silica substrate via flip-chip bonding, yielding a resonance frequency (\(f_s\)) of 7.16 GHz with an extracted \(k_t^2\) of 12.25\% and \(Q\) of 100, facilitating a high \(Q\cdot k_t^2\cdot f_s\) product of 87.71. The results demonstrate strong piezoelectric transduction through a nanoscale air gap, supporting further development of the platform for heterogeneous integration of compact, low-loss microwave components.

items.title: Emotion-Aware Prefix: Towards Explicit Emotion Control in Voice Conversion Models
items.summary: Recent advances in zero-shot voice conversion have exhibited potential in emotion control, yet the performance is suboptimal or inconsistent due to their limited expressive capacity. We propose Emotion-Aware Prefix for explicit emotion control in a two-stage voice conversion backbone. We significantly improve emotion conversion performance, doubling the baseline Emotion Conversion Accuracy (ECA) from 42.40% to 85.50% while maintaining linguistic integrity and speech quality, without compromising speaker identity. Our ablation study suggests that a joint control of both sequence modulation and acoustic realization is essential to synthesize distinct emotions. Furthermore, comparative analysis verifies the generalizability of proposed method, while it provides insights on the role of acoustic decoupling in maintaining speaker identity.

items.title: 20 GHz Longitudinal Surface Acoustic Wave Resonators in 100-nm X-Cut Lithium Niobate on Silicon Carbide
items.summary: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators above 15~GHz require a fast acoustic mode that retains strong electromechanical coupling ($k^2$). This work reports longitudinal SAW (L-SAW) resonators designed for high $k^2$ in 100-nm X-cut lithium niobate (LN) on 4H silicon carbide (SiC), operating up to 21.7~GHz and reaching a $k^2$ of 8.1\%, a maximum Bode $Q$ of 70, and a figure of merit (FoM) of 5.7 at 20.24~GHz. In this thin-film waveguide, shrinking the wavelength ($λ$) keeps the normalized LN thickness ($h_\mathrm{LN}/λ$) large, sustaining both $k^2$ and acoustic confinement. Conversely, increasing $λ$ from 292 to 471~nm lowers $h_\mathrm{LN}/λ$ from 0.34 to 0.21 and raises the L-SAW phase velocity from 6.32 to 7.05~km/s, within 1.1\% of the 7126-m/s shear-wave velocity of 4H-SiC. As the velocity approaches this limit, more of the acoustic energy spreads into the non-piezoelectric SiC, and $k^2$ falls from its 8.1\% peak at $λ= 322$~nm to 1.7\% at $λ= 471$~nm. No L-SAW resonance is observed for $λ\geq 518$~nm ($h_\mathrm{LN}/λ\leq 0.19$), where the mode becomes leaky. Overall, the FoM stays within 5\% of its maximum for $h_\mathrm{LN}/λ$ between 0.26 to 0.31, defining a design window for L-SAW resonators in thin LN on SiC at K-band and beyond.

items.title: Bayesian Bias Learning-Enabled Probabilistic Voltage Estimation with Unknown Uncertainty Modeling of DERs in Distribution Grids
items.summary: One key challenge in distribution system state es- timation is unknown input statistics from the growing inte- gration of distributed energy resources (DERs), which may largely deviate from Gaussian uncertainty. Existing model-based estimators often rely on the assumption that all inputs follow known Gaussian distributions, while data-driven methods suffer from overfitting and failure in out-of-distribution scenarios. This paper proposes a Bayesian bias learning (BBL)-enabled probabilistic voltage estimation method in distribution systems with unknown DER generation statistics. The proposed learning- enabled method consists of two stages: probabilistic uncertainty inference and computationally efficient voltage estimation. First, a physics-constrained probabilistic density inference network is developed to learn Gaussian mixture representations of DER generation from historical data. Then, the resulting probabilistic representations, treated as pseudo-measurements, are integrated into a BBL-enabled voltage estimator via a decomposition- and-parallelization mechanism. Furthermore, utilizing a linear analytical solution, the proposed BBL-enabled voltage estimator efficiently captures linearization-induced biases and attains ac- curate probabilistic estimation. By integrating learning-enabled probabilistic uncertainty modeling into the parallel estimation structure, the proposed method achieves uncertainty-aware scal- able voltage estimation. Case studies on two unbalanced IEEE distribution networks show that the proposed estimator achieves significantly higher accuracy and computational efficiency under unknown uncertainty, outperforming recent data-driven and model-based methods.

items.title: A Spatial Clustering and Resource Allocation Approach for Critical Services in Massive MIMO-Enabled Cellular Networks
items.summary: In this work, we address the challenge of providing quality-of-service (QoS) guarantees for critical real-time services in cellular networks where both real-time and non-real-time applications must be supported. Leveraging the spatial multiplexing capabilities of Massive Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) technology, we propose a joint clustering and resource allocation framework that limits network interference and enhances the ability to meet the QoS requirements of real-time services while still serving other applications. Our approach begins by clustering active users according to the direction of their channel vectors. Specifically, a downlink probing strategy is employed to group users whose channels lie in the same direction. Channel estimation and the derivation of the corresponding signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) are then performed based on this clustering. Subsequently, we formulate a resource allocation optimization problem across the user groups to satisfy the required QoS for critical real-time services while accommodating the remaining users. We rigorously prove that, in general, finding the global optimum of the resource allocation problem is NP-hard, and for a special case of the formulated problem, we establish a polynomial-time solvable algorithm based on linear programming. We then propose a suboptimal solution for the general problem using a linear relaxation technique. Simulation results are provided to confirm the effectiveness of our proposed approaches.

items.title: Simplifying Gas-Phase Kinetic Measurements with a Dual-Arm Flow Tube
items.summary: We demonstrate a simple dual-arm flow tube reactor that provides well-defined reaction times ranging from one second to several minutes for gas-phase kinetic measurements near ambient temperature and pressure. Constructed entirely from standard tubing, the flow tube reactor eliminates the need for injector translation. It operates in two configurations: a variable-length configuration, in which the tube length is changed at fixed flow, and a variable-flow configuration, in which an exhaust branch allows the flow through the reaction section to be adjusted while maintaining constant reactant inlet flows. With 3.96 mm i.d. tubing, the measured tracer pulses had a typical full width at half maximum of about $10\%$ of their mean arrival time. A kinetic demonstration using the ozonolysis of 2,3-dimethyl-2-butene (TME) yields an apparent rate coefficient for TME loss $k_{\mathrm{app}} = 2.0(5) \times 10^{-15}\,\mathrm{cm}^{3}\,\mathrm{molecule}^{-1}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. Fitting the same kinetic data with a reaction network including secondary OH and peroxy-radical chemistry yields $k = 1.18(19) \times 10^{-15}\,\mathrm{cm}^{3}\,\mathrm{molecule}^{-1}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ at 293 K for TME + $\mathrm{O}_{3}$, consistent with the IUPAC recommendation. This compact, low-cost reactor provides an alternative to conventional movable-injector flow tubes for atmospheric chemistry, fundamental kinetics, and gas-liquid or gas-solid uptake studies.

items.title: A Dual-Mode Protocol for Space-Time-Coding Metasurfaces in OFDM ISAC Systems
items.summary: Existing integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) frameworks assisted by space-time-coding metasurfaces (STCMs) rely on idealized surface models, which neglect the frequency-selective and angle-dependent response of the meta-atoms, and are typically limited to narrowband single-carrier communications. This paper addresses these limitations by developing a physics-based signal-processing framework for STCM-assisted ISAC systems employing wideband orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) waveforms, which accounts also for beam squint effects across the STCM aperture. On this basis, we propose a dual-mode protocol, in which the STCM operates as a time-varying surface during a short acquisition phase and as a conventional reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) during data transmission. In the acquisition phase, the angle of arrival (AoA) and the composite channel are jointly estimated by maximum likelihood from a single pilot OFDM symbol transmitted over a subset of active subcarriers, together with deliberately introduced virtual carriers; these estimates are then used to configure the RIS for data transmission. Numerical results validate the considered framework and quantify the gains achievable by the proposed dual-mode protocol.

items.title: Optimal Uniform Pricing for Multi-Interval Dispatch without Make-Whole Uplifts
items.summary: In a network with ramp-limited generators and inaccurate net-demand forecasts, practical rolling-window dispatch can drive locational marginal prices (LMPs) below generators' bid-in offers. In such cases, out-of-market (OOM) settlements are used to compensate generators and maintain dispatch-following incentives, but OOM can have negative consequences, including nontransparent real-time price signals, discriminatory compensation, and incentives for untruthful bidding. This paper presents an optimal uniform pricing rule that minimizes demand payments, eliminates OOM make-whole payments, preserves LMP-based congestion charges, and ensures revenue adequacy. We derive the proposed pricing rule in closed form and relate it to existing pricing schemes. Numerical comparisons demonstrate favorable generator profits and reduced price volatility. However, higher generator profits are accompanied by increased demand payments, reflecting the in-market, uniform allocation of ramping costs while preserving the LMP-based congestion charges widely used in real-time market settlements. The numerical results also show that, under LMP with OOM settlement, a price-taking generator has an incentive to inflate its offer, whereas this incentive is absent under the proposed pricing rule within the tested bid range.

items.title: Eliminating Make-Whole Uplifts with a Minimum-Cost Uniform Price Adder
items.summary: Co-optimizing energy and flexible ramping reserves may dispatch generators at locational marginal prices (LMPs) below their submitted energy offer prices, necessitating out-of-market make-whole payments. Such payments create discriminatory settlements among generators and may incentivize strategic bidding for higher profits. This paper proposes LMP+U, an in-market uniform price adder to LMP for transmission-constrained networks, which minimizes demand payments subject to zero out-of-market make-whole uplift, preserves LMP-based congestion charges, and provides locally truthful bidding incentives for price-taking generators. We also identify conditions under which a price-taking generator can increase its profit by inflating its energy offer under conventional LMP with make-whole uplift. Numerical simulations illustrate the properties of LMP+U and its advantages over conventional LMP in congested networks.

items.title: Iteration-Dependent Temporal Resilience in Diffusion Models for Approximate Computing
items.summary: This paper empirically analyzes iteration-dependent resilience in diffusion models by replacing MACs with efficient SAC approximations. Results on Q-Diffusion show early steps are highly sensitive while later steps are robust, enabling iteration- aware approximation that improves efficiency and reduces hardware cost with minimal quality loss.

items.title: Hierarchical Agentic Mid-Band Agility for Reliable Low-Latency Space-Air-Ground Integrated V2X Networks
items.summary: Upper-mid-band spectrum offers bandwidth opportunities for the integrated networks of ground vehicles, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites to support 6G wide-area vehicle-to-everything (V2X) connectivity. However, V2X services' latency and reliability are sensitive to the mid-band selection due to frequency-dependent propagation and rain attenuation. This paper investigates environment-aware spectrum agility over candidate frequency range 3 (FR3) bands within 7.125-24.25 GHz, jointly with end-to-end (E2E) multi-path traffic splitting and transmit power control. Each data packet is partitioned into non-overlapping subflows over direct and UAV-assisted paths, with failed sky-link subflows selectively retransmitted subject to retransmission and freshness constraints. We formulate latency- and reliability-oriented problems, followed by a unified sequential optimization problem incorporating band-switching costs and average quality-of-service (QoS) violation budgets. To coordinate optimization decisions across heterogeneous timescales, we develop an agentic AI-assisted hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning (AA-HMARL) framework. A high-level agentic supervisor integrates recurrent memory, analytical evaluation of candidate bands, and event-triggered replanning to coordinate slow environmental adaptation with fast channel and retransmission dynamics, while distributed ground vehicles and UAV agents optimize data splitting and power using constrained MAPPO. Simulation results demonstrate an adjustable reliability-latency trade-off. Particularly, AA-HMARL reduces the mean E2E completion latency and the mean number of retransmission rounds among successfully delivered updates by 17.8-25.5% and 57.6-61.5%, respectively, and reduces the mean age of information (AoI) by 12.7-14.6% relative to fixed-band MAPPO across two traffic types.

items.title: Set-Theoretic PAPR Reduction in Multi-Antenna Systems
items.summary: In this study, we propose an optimization framework for PAPR reduction in multi-antenna systems with beamforming. Unlike previous techniques, the proposed approach permits full control over the distorted symbol constellation via arbitrary (convex) constraints on the frequency domain symbols, while minimizing the PAPR at each individual transmit antenna. We propose an iterative algorithm based on an extrapolated alternating projection method, which relies on an iterative soft-thresholding subroutine to compute projections onto sublevel sets of the objective function, and we compare its performance to optimal solutions obtained with general-purpose convex solvers.

items.title: From Tokens to Pixels: Training-Free Guided Upsampling of Frozen CARL Features for Hyperspectral Imaging
items.summary: Camera-agnostic foundation models such as CARL map spectral images from arbitrary sensors into a shared feature space, but deliver their features only on a token grid at one eighth of the input resolution. The usual bilinear interpolation blurs material boundaries over about one token and rounds off corners. We investigate how much spatial accuracy image-guided upsampling recovers for frozen CARL features without training the encoder or the upsampler. We compare joint bilateral upsampling (JBU), a guided filter and the pretrained AnyUp, each with the hyperspectral image or an RGB rendering as the guide. A hyperspectral ColorChecker dataset acquired specifically for this study, with model-independent reference geometry measured to sub-pixel precision, serves as the evaluation benchmark. JBU with the hyperspectral guide raises the Boundary IoU from 13 to 67 % and reduces the effective edge width of the features from 38 to 4 px, close to the resolution of the raw spectra. The effect occurs in all 24 patches of the ColorChecker and replicates on an additional recording. On placenta and oral cavity images, the feature edges also become markedly qualitatively sharper. For sharp, high-contrast boundaries, JBU is the most accurate and most economical method. On tissue with softer transitions, the pretrained AnyUp yields qualitatively sharper contours. An analysis of 78 simulated band configurations shows that the gain persists in every configuration as long as the head matches the configuration. Image-guided upsampling is thus a simple, training-free step for applications that use CARL frozen with linear heads.

items.title: Where Delay Compensation Belongs in a Decentralized Mean-Field-Game Swarm with a Control-Barrier Safety Filter
items.summary: Large robot teams are often run as a plan-then-execute stack. We study a decentralized instance for drone swarms, a mean-field-game (MFG) routing field with a per-agent control-barrier-function (CBF) safety filter, when communication is limited by a shared TDMA channel. Neighbors are known only through noisy range and bearing measurements exchanged in round-robin slots, so the frame, and with it the age of every estimate, grows with swarm size. In simulation this delay reaches both layers but breaks only the safety layer. Without delay, swarms of up to 100 agents do not collide, even with each measurement's noise held for a whole frame; with it, stale estimates at the CBF cause collisions beyond a frame period of 125 to 175 ms, or 75 to 100 ms at 100 agents with held noise, and swarm size sets where that limit lies and how steeply collisions rise. At the MFG, staleness makes the local density noisier without biasing it, and throughput drops by at most a tenth. We then compensate with lightweight on-board predictors, from constant-velocity fits to a small learned network, that estimate each neighbor's position from its last broadcasts. A layer-split experiment shows where prediction is needed: at the CBF it restores safety and extends the tolerated frame period by 1.4 to 1.7 times with an untrained constant-velocity fit and about 2.3 with the learned network when the noise is redrawn each step; with noise held for a frame the two extend it about equally, while at the MFG it only refines the congestion correction. A constant wider safety margin, the simplest alternative, makes collisions more frequent in a bottleneck. With the routing solved offline, that layer is robust to the delay because it sees neighbors only through a crowd average; compensation belongs in the safety filter, switched on only above the uncompensated limit, since below it the predictor's own error adds collisions.

items.title: From Pilots to Position: Experimental Near-Field Localization for ISAC
items.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables wireless systems to reuse communication signals for environmental sensing, potentially reducing the need for dedicated sensing resources. However, the achievable localization accuracy of communication-centric waveforms under practical hardware constraints remains an important challenge. In this paper, we experimentally investigate near-field target localization using OFDM pilot signals in a distributed communication system. We consider both coherent and noncoherent localization approaches, exploiting multistatic propagation delays and time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) information extracted from pilot-based channel estimates. A hardware setup comprising two transmitters and four receivers was developed and configured to operate at 3.4 GHz with 198 MHz occupied bandwidth to evaluate localization performance under realistic propagation and synchronization conditions. Experimental results across 16 static target positions demonstrate mean localization errors of 19.8 cm and 18.8 cm for coherent backprojection and noncoherent delay-TDOA fusion, respectively. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of occupied bandwidth on localization accuracy of the two proposed algorithms. These findings provide experimental insights into the capabilities and practical limitations of OFDM pilot-based sensing, supporting resource-efficient localization in future ISAC systems.

items.title: FlashReFocus: Interactive Image Refocusing in Seconds
items.summary: Single-image refocusing changes the focal plane and depth of field of a photograph after capture. Users compare focal choices on one photograph, so content stability across edits matters alongside quality and speed. Recent generative methods rerun large diffusion models for every edit, even when they first restore an all-in-focus image, so content can change inconsistently between edits. Yet only this restoration is highly ill-posed and benefits from a generative prior, whereas rendering blur is largely determined by depth and the focal plane. We therefore propose FlashReFocus, which runs diffusion once per photograph and renders each edit with a lightweight network. A one-step diffusion deblurrer with a decoder refiner recovers fine detail efficiently while balancing fidelity and perceptual quality. The renderer uses an explicit defocus map for control and defocus-bias attention to promote information exchange between tokens with similar blur magnitudes. Because every edit reuses the same reconstruction, in-focus content stays consistent across edits, and editing the map enables tilt-shift and two-plane effects. We further collect 3CReal, a benchmark of 89 pairs from three camera-lens systems, to evaluate generalization to unseen optics. For zero-shot bokeh rendering on EBB! Val176 and 3CReal, FlashReFocus leads the evaluated methods in fidelity and perceptual quality. At 1536x1536, a complete refocus takes 2.45 s and each subsequent edit 0.46 s on one RTX PRO 6000.

items.title: Efficient Natural Language to Temporal Logic Translation for Real-Time Physical AI
items.summary: Robots can be controlled to perform tasks with guaranteed correctness when the task instructions are stated in a formal language. Large language models (LLMs) have been widely used to allow users to provide such instructions in natural language (NL), by translating NL into formal language. When deploying such translators on a robot, however, we face limited computing and energy resources, while offloading computation or data to the cloud may be infeasible or undesirable. Yet an LLM is a general-purpose text generator, whereas a formula in a fixed formal language fragment follows a well-defined syntax. We therefore ask whether text generation is needed at all. For the formal language of linear temporal logic (LTL), we show that this translation can instead be broken down into answering a set of questions with pre-defined answers. We then construct a System-One model, a recent class of NL-based classifier, to provide such answers and enable us to translate a natural language instruction into an LTL instruction. On three benchmarks, our translator matches or exceeds the accuracy of the best local LLMs available, at up to one order of magnitude lower runtime and energy consumption. We show that it generalizes to unseen atomic propositions and temporal patterns.

items.title: Incentive-based Fleet Rebalancing in Vehicle-Sharing Systems via Equilibrium-Constrained Optimal Control
items.summary: We propose an incentive-based fleet rebalancing scheme for vehicle-sharing systems that uses fare discounts to steer users toward alternative pick-up locations. The discounts solve an optimal control problem that trades off users leaving the service against incentive costs over a day of operation. Users' responses to incentives are modeled as a Nash equilibrium of logit models coupled through shared vehicle-availability constraints, which makes the control problem a mathematical program with nested equilibrium constraints. We develop a first-order algorithm that backpropagates through the equilibria via nonsmooth implicit differentiation and enjoys convergence guarantees. In a case study that uses Helsinki bike-sharing data, our scheme reduces the number of leaving users by up to 99% relative to no incentives, and outperforms heuristic policies while using up to 52% less incentive.

items.title: Beyond Scalar Inertia: Frequency-Response-Based Assessment of Finite-Duration Inertial Support in Grid-Forming Converters
items.summary: Conventional scalar inertia characterizes only the low-frequency terminal behavior of grid-forming converters (GFMs) and cannot fully predict inertial energy delivery during short-duration frequency disturbances. This letter proposes a frequency-response-based method to assess finite-duration inertial support using complex terminal power--frequency responses, such as those provided by Network Frequency Perturbation (NFP) plots. For GFMs with nonzero steady-state droop, a duration-dependent energy-equivalent inertia is defined after subtracting the ideal static-droop contribution. An exact spectral relationship is established, expressing this metric as a duration-weighted integral of frequency-dependent inertia, without requiring knowledge of the internal controller structure and parameters. The duration dependence of the metric is further shown to encode observable oscillation frequencies and damping ratios. A coefficient-decoupling GFM control with identical scalar inertia and droop across different settings is used for verification.

items.title: Learned Network Dynamics for Model Predictive Traffic Signal Control under Incidents
items.summary: Model predictive control (MPC) of urban traffic signals relies on a model of how queues respond to signal decisions, which is hard to specify and calibrate in heterogeneous networks, particularly when incidents change capacities and turning shares. Measurements add a second limitation: the controlled lanes at the stop line are often short, so queues extending upstream of them fall outside lane-level measurements. We propose GNN-MPC, a receding-horizon controller that plans with action-conditioned network dynamics learned by graph neural networks. Phase sequences are coordinated across intersections by approximate best responses, with an acceptance test that keeps the predicted cost no higher than that of the initial plan. In microscopic simulation under non-recurrent incidents, GNN-MPC reduces travel time and increases completed trips relative to all tested controllers, on a homogeneous grid and a heterogeneous 21-intersection network. Controlled comparisons on the heterogeneous network distinguish the roles of observation and prediction. With nearly as many vehicles entering the network, GNN-MPC reduces travel time by 13% relative to MaxPressure with the same upstream measurement, and GNN-MPC without the upstream representation does not reproduce its performance. Under the same traffic measurements, planner and objective, replacing the learned dynamics with calibrated store-and-forward predictors increases travel time by 31-34%. Observing hidden demand and predicting its response to control are thus complementary requirements of network-level predictive control.

items.title: Linear Quadratic Control With Event-Based Control Actions: Performance Beyond Periodic Control
items.summary: This paper investigates linear quadratic (LQ) control for discrete-time stochastic systems to balance control performance and actuation rate. In our framework, the control input is sparse in time, and the actuation timings are determined in an event-based manner. We examine two types of problems: A sparsity-promoting regularization problem and a hard-constraint problem with a prescribed average actuation rate. Due to the combinatorial nature of these problems, finding optimal solutions is generally hard. Inspired by rollout algorithms in the context of dynamic programming, we develop a rollout-based approach to obtain tractable suboptimal policies. We show closed-loop stability and establish theoretical performance guarantees with respect to classical periodic control. Moreover, under additional conditions, we quantify the performance improvement over periodic control and prove that this improvement is strictly positive. A numerical example demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method in balancing control performance and actuation rate.

items.title: Active Learning of Flows from Curve Observations using Gaussian Processes
items.summary: The active learning of real control systems requires informative roll-outs of controls. In this paper, we present a local optimization algorithm that finds the trajectory that most reduces uncertainty about the flow of a control system modeled by a Gaussian process. Therefore, we derive an approximation scheme for the posterior kernel of the Gaussian process after observing it on an entire continuous-time trajectory and establish a Pontryagin-type necessary condition for the optimizer. As the flow is unknown, the actual trajectory can deviate from the planned trajectory. We propose a trajectory planner that searches for the most informative control within a maximal allowed deviation horizon instead of a fixed time horizon. We show by trajectory-wise time rescaling that the underlying optimal control problem is equivalent to a fixed end time optimal control problem. Finally, we study both the fixed end time planner and the fixed maximum deviation planner in a numerical example and compare them with benchmarks.

items.title: Network Traffic Dynamics in Urban Low-Altitude Air Transport with Projected-Space Macroscopic Fundamental Diagrams
items.summary: The growth of Low-Altitude Air Transport (LAAT) systems calls for effective macroscopic modeling tools to manage dense drone traffic. The Macroscopic Fundamental Diagram (MFD) offers a promising framework for this purpose, but its conventional formulations do not directly account for the three-dimensional interactions and path deviations that characterize drone operations. To address this challenge, we introduce a projected-space framework that represents drone motion using projected speed and shortest origin-destination (OD) distances, eliminating the dependence on realized trip lengths that are unknown at trip generation. Under suitable assumptions, we prove the steady-state exactness of the projected-space accumulation-based model and establish deterministic finite-window error bounds for the trip-based estimator. The projected-space accumulation-based formulation is further extended to heterogeneous multi-class systems to accommodate different drone characteristics and operational priorities. Microscopic simulations validate the projected-space formulations under stationary and transient traffic conditions, including hysteresis. Moreover, simulations involving heterogeneous priority classes demonstrate that mixed-priority operations can improve network outflow under the investigated scenarios. These findings establish a theoretical foundation for projected-space macroscopic modeling of LAAT systems and support its application to real-time traffic estimation and future airspace management and control.

items.title: Dual-Agent DRL based Cooperative Beamforming and Trajectory Optimization for UAV-ISAC Networks
items.summary: This paper considers a low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) network, where multiple ground base stations (BSs) provide integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) services for multiple communication UAVs (C-UAVs) and sensing UAVs (S-UAVs). With the objective of maximizing the average sum rate of C-UAVs over the entire flight episode, we jointly optimize the multi-BS multi-UAV ISAC beamforming and trajectory design, subject to the BS transmit power budget and the sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints of S-UAVs, as well as the flight mission and collision avoidance constraints of C-UAVs and S-UAVs. Based on the multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) technique, we develop a dual-agent scheme, termed DeepDA-OPT, to solve the resulting constrained Markov decision process (MDP). In the proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme, two agents, i.e., Agent-B and Agent-T, are specifically deployed for learning the multi-BS ISAC transmit beamformers and the C-UAV/S-UAV trajectories, respectively, where the optimal BS receive beamformers for the sensing echo signals of S-UAVs are obtained in closed form by leveraging the generalized Rayleigh quotient theorem. To mitigate the overestimation of value functions, both Agent-B and Agent-T are trained based on the twin-delayed deep deterministic (TD3) policy-gradient algorithm. In addition, a constraint-aware noise exploration policy is employed, and the reward function is designed to incorporate a sensing penalty and a flight urgency penalty, thereby guiding the training of Agent-B and Agent-T. Numerical results show that, compared with the baseline schemes, the proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme achieves a higher average sum rate of C-UAVs, while the sensing SINR constraints are empirically well satisfied and no collision violation is observed under the evaluated settings.

items.title: Learned Score-Based Turbo Message Passing for Compressive Image Recovery
items.summary: Score-based generative models have been incorpo-rated into message passing algorithms for compressive image recovery, providing a prior for the denoising module in message passing. Score-based generative models assume the input signal to be a clean signal perturbed by independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) Gaussian noise. Yet, this assumption often fails during message passing, leading to slow convergence and limited reconstruction quality. In this letter, we propose the learned score-based turbo message passing (LSTMP) algorithm to overcome this limitation. By employing a deep unfolding framework, LSTMP unrolls the iterative process into a neural network, enabling the denoiser to adapt to complicated noise distributions inherent in the iterative updates. Furthermore, by treating the denoiser as an iterative solver, we incorporate the likelihood information of compressed measurements into the neural network of the denoiser, resembling the message passing between linear and nonlinear modules in STMP. Experiments on the FFHQ dataset show that LSTMP achieves convergence in no more than three iterations while delivering high-ffdelity re-constructions, signiffcantly outperforming the existing baselines.

items.title: On the Existence of Koopman Linear Embeddings for Controlled Nonlinear Systems
items.summary: Koopman linear representations have become a popular tool for control design of nonlinear systems, yet it remains unclear when such representations are exact. In this paper, we establish sufficient and necessary conditions under which a controlled nonlinear system admits an exact Koopman linear representation in both infinite-dimensional and finite-dimensional settings. We show that such a system must be transformable into a special control-affine preserved (CAP) structure, which enforces affine dependence of the state on the control input and isolates all nonlinearities into an autonomous subsystem. We further prove that a finite-dimensional representation additionally requires this autonomous subsystem must itself admit a finite-dimensional Koopman linear model with a sufficiently-rich Koopman invariant subspace. Finally, we introduce a symbolic procedure to determine whether a given controlled nonlinear system admits the CAP structure, thereby elucidating whether Koopman approximation errors arise from intrinsic system dynamics or from the choice of lifting functions.

items.title: PepDeTech: Anonymous Occupancy Monitoring on a Battery-Powered 2.3k-Zone dToF LiDAR Node with On-Chip Processing and Bluetooth LE Reporting
items.summary: As populations grow, society is increasingly required to shift towards systems of shared resources, which allow space, energy and time to be optimised. Facilitating this transition depends on data: how many people are present, when and where. From such information, schedules can be organised more efficiently and resources allocated where they matter. At the same time, privacy concerns and energy consumption limit deployment: cameras are frequently unacceptable, while simpler sensors miss people and cannot provide the full picture. This paper presents PepDeTech, a compact, battery-powered occupancy node that combines a 54 x 42-zone direct Time-of-Flight (dToF) Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) (VL53L9CX) with a Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) System on Chip (SoC). Three deterministic algorithms, background subtraction, motion history and a track lifecycle, run on-chip and count the people simultaneously, providing real-time occupancy monitoring. No trained model is involved, and setup takes less than a minute. Over three scenarios, background subtraction reaches a per-frame +-1-person accuracy of 83.6 % (mean absolute error (MAE) 0.70 persons), tested with up to five people present. At a 30 s interval the node draws only 3.1 mW, lasting 60 d on a 1200 mA h cell. Several weeks of deployment on a single charge make the node usable as a survey instrument for facility management: a room can be characterised for a measurement campaign without cabling, network provisioning or a camera, and the resulting occupancy record is what ventilation, lighting, cleaning and space-allocation decisions are argued from, ultimately resulting in more efficient resource allocation.

items.title: Strong Functional Observability and Strong Functional Detectability: Applications to Functional Observer Design for Systems with Unknown Inputs
items.summary: This paper investigates strong functional observability, strong functional detectability, and strong$^*$ functional detectability for continuous-time linear systems with unknown inputs in both the state and measurement equations. Extending Kratz's finite algebraic approach \cite{26}, zero-output trajectories are characterized through the projected kernel of a finite matrix, without differentiating the unknown inputs. This characterization yields a necessary and sufficient rank condition for strong functional observability. For strong functional detectability, a frequency-dependent rank criterion involving only the original system matrices is derived, along with an equivalent finite test based on reduced zero-output dynamics. Strong$^*$ functional detectability is then characterized by an additional algebraic rank condition, and its relationship with the existence of stable functional observers is examined. A constructive observer design procedure based on constrained Sylvester equations is also developed. Particular cases and a numerical process example illustrate the theoretical results.

items.title: InterBand-EMG: A Cross-Band Foundation Model for Generalizable Hand-Pose Estimation
items.summary: Surface electromyography (sEMG) enables continuous hand-pose estimation, but learning representations that generalize across users and movements remains challenging. We introduce InterBand-EMG, which combines band-specific quantization with cross-band reconstruction and structured masked code prediction to learn transferable EMG representations for hand-pose tracking. We also introduce SynapMyo, an eight-channel EMG-to-pose dataset comprising 1,227.74 hand-hours from 499 users across 68 movement categories. Experiments on emg2pose and SynapMyo show that InterBand-EMG outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in joint-angle accuracy across all three generalization settings on both datasets. The source code and the SynapMyo dataset will be publicly released upon acceptance of this paper.

items.title: Error-Corrected Physics-Informed Neural Operator for Optimal Control of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles under Uncertainty
items.summary: We solve open-loop optimal control problems under parametric uncertainty using a physics-informed DeepONet that returns trajectories for all sampled scenarios in one evaluation. Trained only on the residual at generic controls, the operator is reused across targets and horizons. Because a gradient-based optimizer exploits surrogate errors, we correct the prediction by one Newton step on the dynamics, computed for all scenarios and times by one parallel scan. The corrected state has a second-order error bounded by the residual alone, and the corrected cost is honest for every control up to the sampling error. On a fixed-wing UAV benchmark, the corrected operator matches the accuracy of a batched Adam solver and an Ipopt solver at equal sample size and is 8 times faster than the Adam solver on the same GPU at a few hundred scenarios and 15 times faster than Ipopt on a CPU.

items.title: ECG-LabWAS: A Laboratory-Wide Association Study Using a Fine-Tuned Single-Lead Electrocardiogram Foundation Model
items.summary: Laboratory testing guides clinical diagnosis but requires blood sampling and processing. The electrocardiogram (ECG) is fast and noninvasive and may carry information about laboratory abnormalities, yet most AI-ECG models target one test at a time using 12-lead recordings. We conducted an exploratory ECG laboratory-wide association study (ECG-LabWAS), fine-tuning an ECG foundation model pretrained on 10.8 million ECGs to screen 50 laboratory tests from single-lead waveforms alone. The model was developed in an emergency-department cohort (MC-MED; 31,826 patients) and applied unchanged to an independent hospital cohort (MIMIC-IV; 115,921 patients). Of 89 abnormality directions (low or high values of each test), 33 met the same screening criteria in both cohorts. Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve in the two cohorts were 0.841 and 0.838 for elevated NT-proBNP, 0.769 and 0.740 for elevated cardiac troponin, 0.755 and 0.731 for elevated creatinine, and 0.713 and 0.710 for low potassium. Discrimination changed little when the ECG--laboratory matching window was widened from $\pm$1 to $\pm$24 hours. Model predictions reproduced the co-occurrence of observed abnormalities but were about twice as tightly coupled, largely along one shared component consistent with overall illness severity; low potassium, elevated NT-proBNP and troponin, and markers of renal function retained discrimination beyond that of correlated tests. In exploratory analyses, ECG-assisted versions of the modified Glasgow Prognostic Score and the systemic inflammatory response syndrome criteria were associated with in-hospital and one-year mortality. These results identify which laboratory abnormalities warrant analyte-specific study with single-lead ECG.

items.title: Recursive Bayesian Monitoring of SLAM Failures for LiDAR-Based UAV Navigation
items.summary: SLAM failures remain difficult to avoid in autonomous robotic systems, and undetected failures can propagate to unsafe planning, control, and mission-level decisions. Existing monitoring strategies often depend on prior maps, estimator-internal variables, or redundant sensing, which limits their applicability to deployed and resource-constrained robots. This paper presents a scene-geometry consistency monitor for detecting geometry-manifested SLAM failures using only the geometric output of the SLAM backend. The targeted failures include cumulative drift-induced failures, abrupt misregistration failures, and backend map corruption when they become observable as inconsistency in reconstructed scene geometry. The proposed method represents revisited local regions with recursive latent voxel geometry and evaluates each current observation against a trusted continuation explanation and a weak non-propagated reference explanation. The resulting voxel-wise evidence contrasts are aggregated into a fixed-boundary monitoring signal for online failure declaration and downstream safety response. Experiments on self-collected sequences, GEODE benchmark sequences, multiple robotic platforms, and different SLAM backends show that the monitor responds to failures when they are manifested in backend scene geometry. It achieves 4/4 valid post-onset declarations with no pre-onset alarms on four self-collected sequences, detects geometry-manifested failures in all five corrupted GEODE runs while remaining alarm-free in five geometrically consistent runs, adds only 0.1--0.2\% absolute CPU load, and supports a closed-loop UAV detect--isolate--recover workflow.

items.title: Dem2TA: Beyond Pixels, Towards Perception
items.summary: Task-oriented image signal processors (ISPs) adapt RAW-to-RGB processing for downstream perception. However, explicit demosaicing is often simplified, kept fixed, or optimized primarily for reconstruction quality, leaving this stage insufficiently integrated into task adaptation. We propose \textbf{Dem2TA}, a framework that incorporates fidelity-supervised demosaicing into the adaptation of the perception pipeline. Starting from a pretrained demosaicing model, we jointly adapt the reconstruction frontend and downstream network using reconstruction and task supervision, together with complementary semantic and task representation alignment. We then freeze the adapted frontend and jointly optimize a lightweight local ISP with the downstream model to refine task-specific rendering without changing the reconstructed linear RGB. Experiments on synthetic RAW detection and box-prompted segmentation demonstrate the effectiveness of representation-guided joint adaptation and subsequent local rendering. Evaluation on a manually verified real-capture dataset further supports transfer beyond synthetic inputs. Compared with TA-ISP on the same adapted foundation, Dem2TA improves detection AP by 0.46 points and segmentation IoU by 1.06 points on synthetic COCO RAW, and segmentation IoU by 0.63 points on real captures.

items.title: Hybrid-Field Interference Suppression for Low-Complexity Uplink Channel Estimation
items.summary: Uplink channel estimation can be severely degraded by hybrid-field interference, where strong near-field intra-site interference is coupled with far-field inter-site interference. Although a joint near-/far-field dictionary can capture this interference structure, it requires dense angle--distance matching that may incur high complexity and performance degradation. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid-field interference suppression framework for uplink channel estimation. First, we formulate a hybrid-field interference model and analyze its sparse reconstruction. Then, to avoid exhaustive near-field dictionary matching, we propose a low-complexity interference-parameter estimation method based on the angle--domain diffusion pattern of the dominant interference. Using the estimated parameters, the proposed parametric interference-nulling orthogonal matching pursuit (PIN-OMP) algorithm suppresses the dominant interference components and reconstructs the desired uplink channel from the interference-suppressed observation. Furthermore, a physical critical-distance bound is derived to characterize the feasible distance-inversion region, and a conditional hybrid Cram'er--Rao bound (HCRB) is established to quantify the desired channel reconstruction limit under a reconstructed interference basis. Finally, numerical results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

items.title: Which Data-Center Load Models Can Be Trusted? An Evidence-Graded Review of Dynamic Modeling and Validation for Large Computational Loads
items.summary: Grid operators now require dynamic models of data centers and other large computational loads, and new ride-through rules assume that these models predict how facilities respond to disturbances. This review asks what evidence supports that assumption. We coded 160 documents, screened from 1,424 de-duplicated database and seed records plus 65 added documents, by the strongest reference object each presents, from grid-side records to simulation only. Across 19 field-evidence entries, 15 requirement documents from three continents and nine model classes, we find two comparisons of a standard library model with measured data-center events: with default parameters the model failed both, and refitting it to each event separately reduced the error but was never tested on an unseen event. Among the sources reviewed, we found no successful held-out validation of a frozen, facility-specific data-center model against an independent measured disturbance, and 25 of the 33 model-phenomenon combinations with any evidence involve no electrical measurement. The features that distinguish the new rules (memory of repeated dips, recovery within 0.5-3 s, proportional power reduction during the sag, overvoltage response) are those current phasor models cannot represent or have never been tested against. In the operator procedures examined, simulations and model-to-model benchmarks are accepted as evidence of model fidelity, unlike the measured validation required of generators, and proposed mitigations have mostly been evaluated on unvalidated facility models. We propose context-of-use gates that separate calibration from validation, release labels for model claims, a minimum validation protocol with acceptance criteria, and a research agenda.

items.title: FM4SAR-Bench 1.0: Towards A Fair Benchmark for Evaluating Foundation Models for SAR Image Interpretation
items.summary: Foundation models have advanced SAR image interpretation but created a heterogeneous, fragmented model ecosystem. Existing models differ substantially in their input, training data, objectives, architectures, and release policy, yet the field lacks a unified taxonomy and comparative framework. Current evaluations rely primarily on task-specific benchmarks, which are ill-suited to fair comparison among models with fundamentally different input-output formats and task paradigms, and often overlook data transparency, reproducibility, interpretability, and deployment readiness. Limited SAR data accessibility also means high reported performance does not guarantee access to training data, code, or weights, limiting reproduction, benchmarking, and deployment. To address these issues, we propose a systematic taxonomy and hierarchical evaluation framework for SAR-related foundation models: five rating levels, six dimensions, and fine-grained criteria, with separate protocols for VFMs and VLMs. Beyond overall ratings, it yields interpretable multidimensional capability profiles and supports user-defined weighting, so rankings follow user priorities. Utilizing a fixed auxiliary multimodal large language model in combination with human review, we conduct a systematic meta-analysis and multidimensional assessment of 76 VFMs and 40 VLMs. In terms of SAR benchmark task performance under our framework, SAR-native VLMs do not significantly outperform remote sensing VLMs pretrained on mixed multimodal corpora in which SAR is one of several modalities. This lack of clear advantage is largely due to data availability: large-scale, high-quality, public annotated SAR data remain scarce, restricting both model and training-data scale for SAR-native models. The framework provides a structured basis for requirement-aware model selection and remains extensible as new models emerge.

items.title: Performance guarantees for optimization-based state estimation using turnpike properties
items.summary: In this paper, we develop novel accuracy and performance guarantees for optimal state estimation of general nonlinear systems (in particular, moving horizon estimation, MHE). Our results rely on a turnpike property of the optimal state estimation problem, which essentially states that the omniscient infinite-horizon solution involving all past and future data serves as turnpike for the solutions of finite-horizon estimation problems involving a subset of the data. This leads to the surprising observation that MHE problems naturally exhibit a leaving arc, which may have a strong negative impact on the estimation accuracy. To address this, we propose a delayed MHE scheme, and we show that the resulting performance (both averaged and non-averaged) is approximately optimal and achieves bounded regret with respect to the infinite-horizon solution, with error terms that can be made arbitrarily small by an appropriate choice of the delay. In various simulation examples, we observe that already a very small delay in the MHE scheme is sufficient to significantly improve the overall estimation error by 20-25% compared to standard MHE (without delay). This finding is of great importance for practical applications (especially for monitoring, fault detection, and parameter estimation) where a small delay in the estimation is rather irrelevant but may significantly improve the estimation results.

items.title: Geometry-Preserving Neural Architectures on Manifolds with Boundary
items.summary: A growing number of neural architectures have been developed to enforce geometric constraints, including projection-based networks, exponential-map updates, and manifold neural ODEs. In this paper, we study several such architectures, with the goal of understanding their approximation-theoretic properties and trade-offs. We distinguish between architectures that enforce constraints at intermediate layers and those that enforce constraints only at the output. For projected neural ODEs on uniformly prox-regular sets, we establish stability estimates and derive universal approximation results on compact smooth manifolds, including manifolds with boundary. In particular, we establish universal approximation of measurable manifold-valued maps in the $L^2$ topology. In contrast, architectures that enforce constraints only at the output can admit uniform approximation guarantees for continuous target maps under suitable geometric assumptions. We further investigate how the choice of constraint-enforcing map, namely metric projection or the Riemannian exponential map, affects these guarantees. While both constructions can be used to preserve constraints at intermediate layers, their use at the output leads to different approximation properties. In particular, exponential-map output architectures can encounter topological obstructions to uniform approximation, motivating approximation guarantees in $L^2$. On the other hand, metric projection-based output architectures can retain uniform approximation guarantees when the constraint set has positive reach. Our study raises the broader question of when the additional complexity of enforcing constraints at intermediate layers, as motivated by neural ODE approaches, and different choices of constraint-enforcing map are justified by the resulting benefits in approximation and learning performance.

items.title: Ace! Motion Planning of Professional-Level Table Tennis Serves with a Robot Arm
items.summary: Table tennis, a dynamic, compact, and popular sport, has for many years received significant attention as a robotics benchmark. Most of the research has focused on the rally aspect -returning an incoming ball-requiring high-speed vision, agile motion planning, and tight closed-loop control. On the other hand, getting robots to serve competitively remains a rather unexplored research problem, which in fact requires pushing physics modeling and control to the extremes. In this work, we present the first-ever approach capable of generating official rule-compliant serves that produce ball spins of up to 550 rad/s and speeds of up to 6.7 m/s, matching and even surpassing the capabilities of elite table tennis players. In official matches against these competitors, our serves score direct points in up to 21% of attempts and push the win rate of robot-initiated rallies above 50%. The motion plans for serving are generated in simulation by combining optimization-based control and Bayesian optimization, and are executed zero-shot in open-loop on our hardware.

items.title: Particle picking with an earth mover's seminorm
items.summary: Particle picking is a key step in single-particle cryo-electron microscopy. It is a challenging task where tomographic projections of proteins and other macromolecules are identified in extremely noisy images. In this work, we introduce a particle picker based on a seminorm defined in terms of a fast wavelet approximation to the earth mover's distance. Our picker is template-free, self-supervised and does not require any prior knowledge of the molecules of interest other than their approximate size. We test it on three public datasets and show that it achieves state-of-the-art reconstructions.

items.title: Mode Recommendation and Dynamic Routing Guidance for Improved Trip Quality in Mixed Traffic Networks
items.summary: Urban mixed traffic networks provide diverse mobility options, yet conventional routing guidance with fixed travel modes leaves the benefits of coordinating travel modes and route planning largely unexploited. This paper proposes an integrated mode recommendation and dynamic routing guidance framework for urban mixed traffic networks comprising private vehicles, autonomous vehicles, and buses. We formulate a dynamic trip index (DTX) that incorporates mode-specific travel time, monetary cost, and convenience, enabling consistent evaluation of trip quality across travel modes. Using this measure, we develop a mode recommendation method that selects feasible autonomous vehicle or bus services based on predicted DTX for travelers without private vehicles, while preserving service capacity for travelers with known demand. We integrate this method with dynamic routing guidance for private and autonomous vehicles to improve the average trip quality of all travelers. Simulation studies involving $1{,}500$ travelers on a real-world road network in Shanghai, China, show that the proposed framework increases the mean realized DTX by $13.01\%$ compared with dynamic routing guidance alone and by $19.68\%$ compared with fixed travel modes with preplanned routes, highlighting the value of mode flexibility in improving trip quality beyond route adaptation.

items.title: Seabird-Aware Multi-Objective Offshore Wind Capacity Allocation: A Gippsland Case Study
items.summary: Offshore wind planning requires balancing capital cost, wind-resource potential, and seabird exposure. We formulate a spatial tri-objective mixed-integer linear program for offshore wind capacity allocation, minimizing capital cost and modeled seabird exposure while maximizing wind-weighted capacity. Applied to Australia's Gippsland offshore wind area, the model identifies exposure reductions of 23-44% at capital-cost premiums of 0.8-6.1% across 15 wind-weighted capacity requirements. We benchmark exposure-aware optimization against 19 percentile-based exclusion thresholds. At a fixed wind-weighted capacity requirement, the 5th-percentile threshold reduces exposure by 30.1% at a 37.6% cost premium, versus at least 30.1% at a 1.4% premium with optimization. Under a fixed capital budget, exclusion screening reduces exposure by 48.2% with a 26.9% capacity loss, compared with 48.5% and 7.6%, respectively, under optimization. These results highlight the value of explicitly optimizing graded seabird exposure.

items.title: On Pareto-Optimal Estimation-Information Limits-Achieving Distributions for Integrated Sensing and Communications
items.summary: ISAC systems enable simultaneous data transmission and environmental sensing using a common waveform. Characterizing their fundamental estimation-information performance limits is of core interest in information theory. In this paper, the achievable data rate for communications and the Miller-Chang-type CRB on sensing distortion are adopted as ISAC performance metrics, both of which are functionals of the ISAC waveform distribution. Our aim is to characterize the optimal input distributions across the entire CRB-rate Pareto boundary, corresponding to different sensing-communication tradeoff preferences. Three types of power constraint on input waveform are considered, namely, i) general power (GP), ii) maximum amplitude (MA), and iii) constant modulus (CM) constraints. Under these constraints, Pareto-optimal input distributions are shown to exhibit a common structural property: the directional component is uniformly distributed over the complex unit sphere; the power distribution is discrete (excluding the communication-optimal point under GP, where it follows a Gamma distribution induced by Gaussian inputs). We further investigate and characterize their Pareto-optimal sensing-communication preference dependent support structures. Finally, numerical algorithms are developed under GP and MA to trace their Pareto boundaries and determine corresponding optimal power distributions based on their respective support characteristics. From both analytical and numerical results, we conclude sensing prefers deterministic power while communication benefits from a richer distribution of power levels, thereby revealing the sensing-communication waveform uncertainty tradeoff in the fundamental power domain.

items.title: Loop-OPF: Solver-Informed Learning for Optimal Power Flow with Inference-Time Topology Adaptivity
items.summary: Learning for optimal power flow (OPF) has recently been advocated to accelerate OPF solutions by using a pre-trained neural network (NN) to predict directly from given inputs such as the load demand. However, existing learning-for-OPF methods largely fall short of ensuring the optimality and feasibility of their predictions. They also struggle to adapt at inference time to unseen topology scenarios, such as those caused by line or generator outages. This work puts forth Loop-OPF, a solver-informed NN that builds its layers from the iterations of the primal-dual hybrid gradient (PDHG) method. Under standard convexity and regularity conditions on DC-OPF, the resultant fixed-point output of Loop-OPF is thus optimal and feasible. To speed up PDHG across diverse OPF scenarios, Loop-OPF learns certain PDHG parameters in a self-supervised manner, without any OPF solution labels. We adopt the deep equilibrium (DEQ) framework for training so that the memory cost does not grow with the number of layers. As the grid topology enters every layer as an input, the same trained Loop-OPF directly adapts to unseen contingencies without retraining. Numerical tests on the IEEE 300-bus and PEGASE 1354-, 2869-, and 9241-bus networks have demonstrated the accuracy and topology adaptivity of the proposed Loop-OPF over competing learning-for-OPF methods.

items.title: Opportunistic Cooperative Sensing in mmWave ISAC Networks: A Meta-Distribution Analysis
items.summary: We propose an opportunistic cooperative sensing architecture for millimeter-wave (mmWave) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks that harvests bistatic echoes from already-active transmissions of neighboring base stations (BSs). Each target is sensed by its nearest BS, while neighboring BSs contribute only when their scheduled beams opportunistically illuminate the target. Cooperation requires neither beam reconfiguration nor dedicated air-interface resources and can leverage existing 5G transport and edge-computing infrastructure for synchronization and local echo processing. Using stochastic geometry, we characterize the sensing meta-distribution for cooperative ISAC, quantifying target-level reliability beyond spatial averages when multiple cooperative echoes are combined, while also analyzing sensing and communication coverage and ergodic rates. Results show that opportunistic cooperation substantially improves average sensing performance and target-level reliability. For instance, at a sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) threshold of 5 dB, increasing the maximum cooperative-cluster size from 1 to 6 raises the percentage of targets whose conditional sensing success probability exceeds 90% by over 55 percentage points. The results further reveal practical design tradeoffs in cluster sizing, BS densification, and sensing-communication energy allocation.

items.title: A Survey of Advancing Audio Super-Resolution and Bandwidth Extension from Discriminative to Generative Models
items.summary: Audio super-resolution (SR), also referred to as bandwidth extension (BWE), aims to reconstruct high-fidelity signals from low-resolution (LR) or band-limited (BL) observations, an inherently ill-posed task due to the ambiguity of missing high-frequency (HF) content. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of the field, with a particular focus on the paradigm shift from discriminative mapping to modern generative modeling. We first review early discriminative deep neural network (DNN) models, which formulate BWE/SR as a deterministic mapping problem and are prone to regression-to-the-mean effects and spectral over-smoothing. We then systematically review generative approaches, including autoregressive (AR) models, variational autoencoders (VAEs), generative adversarial networks (GANs), diffusion and score-based models, flow-based methods, and Schrödinger bridges. Across these approaches, we examine key design aspects, including representation domain, architecture, conditioning mechanisms, and trade-offs among reconstruction fidelity, perceptual quality, robustness, and computational efficiency. We further conduct unified experiments on representative discriminative and generative methods to provide controlled empirical evidence for these trade-offs. Furthermore, we discuss emerging directions involving large language models (LLMs) and multimodal foundation models, and highlight open challenges in perceptual evaluation, practical deployment, and real-world generalization. By providing a structured taxonomy and unified perspective, this survey establishes a comprehensive foundation and offers a practical roadmap for advancing BWE/SR from deterministic point estimation toward distribution-aware generative modeling.

items.title: Reference-Filter-Driven Transition Probabilities for IMM-Based Satellite Maneuver Detection
items.summary: Detecting maneuvers of non-cooperative satellites is essential for space situational awareness. The interacting multiple model (IMM) filter has been applied to detect unannounced maneuvers, but the standard IMM assumes a fixed Markov transition probability matrix (TPM) that must be tuned without knowledge of the maneuver rate of the target. To avoid the tuning, adaptive-TPM approaches update the TPM online from statistics computed inside the IMM. However, the statistics already depend on the TPM through the interaction step, and the dependence forms a feedback loop. The loop itself can raise the maneuver probability in the absence of a maneuver or suppress its rise when a maneuver occurs. In this paper, the TPM is driven by the normalized innovation squared (NIS) of a reference coast filter that is decoupled from the IMM, and the NIS is mapped continuously to the coast-to-maneuver transition probability. The reference-driven IMM (RD-IMM) is evaluated with four space-based optical sensors tracking a geostationary target. In the simulation, the reference filter keeps its sensitivity after small maneuvers, whereas the NIS of the coast sub-filter of the IMM is reduced by the interaction step. RD-IMM detects 1-3 m/s maneuvers, which the fixed-TPM IMM rarely detects, with a false-declaration rate below the false-alarm probability of 0.05 set for the reference filter. In the first hour after the 1-3 m/s maneuvers, RD-IMM also has a lower position error than the compared filters.

items.title: UNILocPro: Unified Localization Integrating Model-Based Geometry and Channel Charting
items.summary: In this paper, we propose a unified framework (called UNILocPro) that integrates model-based geometry and channel charting (CC) for localization via a single massive multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) base station (BS) in mixed line-of-sight (LoS)/non-line-of-sight (NLoS) scenarios. Specifically, based on LoS/NLoS identification, an adaptive activation between the model-based and CC-based methods is conducted. Aiming for unsupervised learning, information obtained from the model-based method is utilized to train the CC model, where a pairwise distance loss (involving a new dissimilarity metric design), a triplet loss (if timestamps are available), a LoS-based loss, and an optimal transport (OT)-based loss are jointly employed such that the global geometry can be well preserved. To reduce the training complexity, we propose a low-complexity implementation (called UNILoc), where the CC model is trained with self-generated labels produced by a single pre-training OT transformation, which avoids iterative Sinkhorn updates involved in the OT-based loss computation. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed unified frameworks achieve significantly improved positioning accuracy compared to both model-based and CC-based methods. Notably, UNILocPro with timestamps attains performance on par with fully-supervised fingerprinting despite operating without labelled training data. It is also shown that the low-complexity UNILoc can substantially reduce training complexity with marginal performance degradation.
