The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified using the 10-adult cohort from the FDA-accepted UVA/Padova T1DM simulator, and an advisory mode analysis is also conducted based on the clinical data from 40 type 1 diabetes and 55 type 2 diabetes subjects to indicate the safe and physiologically plausible decisions in the real-life applications.

items.title: TELEVAL: A Benchmark Designed for Spoken Language Models in Chinese Interactive Scenarios
items.summary: Spoken Language Models (SLMs) are expected to support natural spoken interaction beyond task completion. Existing benchmarks assess a range of semantic tasks and conversational capabilities. However, high task scores do not necessarily imply reliable and appropriate spoken interaction. To address this gap, we introduce TELEVAL, a large-scale benchmark focused on Chinese spoken interaction. It evaluates responses to spoken inputs without additional task-specific prompts or predefined answer options. TELEVAL covers two complementary aspects: (1) Reliable Content Fulfillment, which measures semantic accuracy under diverse acoustic and linguistic conditions, and (2) Interactional Appropriateness, which assesses conversational naturalness and appropriate adaptation to auditory cues. Experiments reveal limitations in both aspects. Strong results on factual question-answering datasets do not consistently extend to locally relevant knowledge or challenging speech conditions, such as Chinese cultural questions and dialectal speech. Models also struggle to adapt their responses to auditory cues, even in cases where they explicitly recognize them. We further document a recurring failure pattern, termed the "Caption Trap", in which some responses describe a perceived auditory cue instead of addressing the user's conversational needs. Overall, the evaluated SLMs struggle to deliver consistently accurate and conversationally appropriate responses. TELEVAL provides a diagnostic framework for evaluating both content reliability and conversational adaptation.

items.title: Coordinated Offloading: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for the Edge-Cloud Continuum
items.summary: The increasing demand for intelligent, low-latency services in edge-cloud continuum systems poses new challenges for dynamic and efficient task offloading. We propose a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework for distributed task offloading under partial observability, where each device offloads only a portion of its computation to a target edge server while executing the remaining portion locally (partial offloading). The problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), where each device independently learns an optimal policy under partially observable system states. To address the non-convexity, high-dimensional state space, and continuous action space, we develop a multi-agent Advantage-Weighted Actor-Critic (AWAC)-enhanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based computation offloading algorithm. The proposed method combines the stable policy updates of PPO with an advantage-weighting mechanism inspired by AWAC to emphasize higher-quality actions during training. To encourage cooperation without inter-device communication, a shared global reward aligned with system cost is employed. Extensive simulations demonstrate rapid convergence and significant improvement in overall system cost compared with baselines, e.g., Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) and Deep Q-Network (DQN).

items.title: Lower Bound of Networked Control with Multiple Sensors and One Controller And The Application to the Side Information Case
items.summary: This paper studies the tradeoff between the communication rate and the control performance for the Linear Quadratic Gaussian(LQG) plant with multiple sensors/encoders and one decoder/controller. Assuming the use of prefix codes for each encoder, we show a causally conditioned directed information lower bound and the sufficiency of a class of linear policies for optimizing this weighted sum lower bound with the full observation condition, reducing it to a finite-dimensional optimization problem. We then apply our analysis to the point-to-point case with side information(SI) at the decoder only, which can be viewed as an extreme case for the multi-encoder setting. We recover the structure result for the sequential rate-distortion function(SRDF) for the point-to-point case with SI. We further present semidefinite programming (SDP) formulations for a broader class of system parameters that recover the past forms as special cases, and show an equivalent single-letter SDP form for the infinite-horizon time-invariant system under certain conditions.

items.title: Massive MIMO-OFDM ISAC for Sparse ISAR Imaging: Joint Power and Subcarrier Allocation
items.summary: This paper investigates a massive multiple-input multiple-output (mMIMO) orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) framework for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) with inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging. A dual-function architecture combines communication precoding and dedicated sensing beamforming to support simultaneous downlink communication and ISAR imaging. To address incomplete measurements arising from intermittent pilot transmission and sparse sensing-subcarrier activation, an adaptive reweighted two-dimensional alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm is developed for sparse ISAR reconstruction. A joint resource-allocation framework is formulated to optimize communication-subcarrier assignment, sensing-subcarrier selection, and transmit power allocation under communication quality-of-service (QoS) and sensing constraints. Exploiting channel hardening, analytical full-band benchmarks based on statistical channel state information (CSI) are derived for maximum-ratio (MR) and zero-forcing (ZF) precoding, while a soft actor-critic (SAC) algorithm is developed for sparse-sensing resource allocation. Numerical results demonstrate that the adaptive ADMM algorithm improves ISAR reconstruction accuracy over conventional methods, while the SAC-based design achieves higher sum spectral efficiency than both the analytical full-band ISAC benchmarks and the deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) baseline under both MR and ZF precoding, while satisfying the communication QoS and sensing constraints.

items.title: Robust SAC-Enabled UAV-RIS Assisted Secure MISO Systems With Untrusted EH Receivers
items.summary: Secure downlink transmission in UAV-mounted reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted multi-user multiple-input single-output (MISO) networks is challenged by imperfect channel state information (CSI), internal eavesdropping by untrusted energy-harvesting receivers (UEHRs), discrete RIS phase shifts, and nonlinear energy harvesting (EH). This paper jointly optimizes the UAV hovering position, base station (BS) transmit power allocation, and discrete RIS phase shifts to maximize the worst-case secrecy energy efficiency (WCSEE) under bounded CSI uncertainty and nonlinear EH constraints. The resulting problem is a highly non-convex mixed-integer fractional optimization problem with tightly coupled spatial, power, and RIS variables. To address these challenges, we develop two complementary solution frameworks. First, for perfect CSI and continuous RIS phase shifts, we derive an analytical benchmark based on block coordinate descent (BCD) and successive convex approximation (SCA). Second, for the general robust setting with discrete phase quantization and CSI uncertainty, we propose a customized soft actor-critic (SAC) framework that incorporates continuous-to-discrete action projection, twin critics to mitigate value overestimation, and a feasibility-aware reward mechanism. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed SAC policy achieves up to $28\%$, $16\%$, and $6\%$ higher WCSEE than the SCA benchmark, DDPG, and TD3, respectively, while exhibiting faster convergence and maintaining stable performance across varying user densities, UEHR counts, and CSI uncertainty levels.

items.title: DISC: A Deterministic Instantaneous-SINR Combiner for Uplink Massive MIMO Systems
items.summary: Future Massive MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output) systems will fit more antennas into compact arrays, making minimum mean-square-error (MMSE) combining computationally demanding. Maximum-ratio (MR) combining serves as a cheaper alternative but performs poorly in multi-user scenarios. Existing solutions to this either mimic the MMSE combiner using second-order statistics or, as in the optimal bilinear equalizer (OBE), rely on the loose use-and-then-forget (UaTF) bound. In this paper, we propose DISC, a novel receive combiner that instead maximizes a deterministic approximation of the instantaneous signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), obtained by replacing the random terms in the SINR with deterministic equivalents. This approximation becomes increasingly accurate as the number of antennas grows, and it exploits useful information discarded by the UaTF bound. The computational complexity of DISC matches that of OBE, with the low-complexity variant DISC-D being even cheaper than conventional MR combining. We further prove that the SINR achieved by DISC grows unbounded with the number of antennas, even under pilot contamination, similarly to MMSE combining. Finally, we numerically demonstrate that DISC achieves a sum spectral efficiency close to that of MMSE combining under full pilot sharing, while outperforming other combiners across signal-to-noise ratio, pilot length, and spatial correlation models.

items.title: A Generative AI-Enhanced Digital Twin Framework for Proactive Interference Management in Hybrid Near/Far-Field Wireless Systems
items.summary: The applications of Digital Twins (DTs) and Generative AI (GenAI) have demonstrated significant potential for modeling and learning-based wireless communications. However, their joint potential for proactive wireless system design remains largely underexplored, particularly in extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) networks characterized by hybrid near-field (NF) and far-field (FF) propagation. In this work, we propose an integrated GenAI-enhanced DT framework for proactive interference management in dynamic indoor environments. The DT constructs a site-specific virtual replica of the deployment, enabling geometry-aware modeling of blockage and hybrid NF/FF propagation. Conditioned on the DT environment and historical network states, GenAI generates multiple plausible future channel and blockage realizations, which are incorporated into regime-aware proactive beamforming. Extensive Sionna ray-tracing simulations across open and cluttered indoor environments, including different user equipment (UE) speeds, demonstrate improved interference suppression, signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), and prediction accuracy compared with reactive and deterministic DT-based benchmarks.

items.title: Modeling and Link Budget Feasibility Analysis of Secure LoRa-Based Peer-to-Peer Communication for Short-Range Tactical Networks
items.summary: Short-range reliable and secure communication is a major priority in the tactical, military and disaster response settings where the traditional communication infrastructure is either off-line or prone to interception. Current VHF/UHF radios and software-defined radios are popular but large-sized devices and require lots of power, making them not suitable to be used as lightweight wearable devices with seamless hand-free use. In this paper, the design and theoretical framework of a miniature, LoRa based encrypted intercommunication device that can be used in secure field communication over a range of 1-1.5km and under line-of-sight conditions is provided. The suggested system consists of a voice-activated acquisition block, digital audio compression, an embedded microcontroller processor, and AES-128 encryption followed by a low-power transmission via the LoRa protocol. Through the ability of chirp spread spectrum modulation to utilize the long-range and low-energy properties, the system is guaranteed reliable communications coupled with low power consumption and low electromagnetic footprint. The theoretical analysis of the proposed communication range is justified using a link-budget that justifies the practicability of the communication range in the real propagation conditions. This architecture focuses on infrastructural agnosticism, peer-to-peer security as well as wearable ergonomics. The given scheme shows the possibilities of LoRa technology in the scope of other traditional IoT telemetry, and it can be further extended to include secure tactical voice communication platforms.

items.title: Dynamic Coordination of Autonomous Vehicles at Intersections
items.summary: The coordination of autonomous vehicles at unsignalized intersections requires deciding both the trajectories of the vehicles and their crossing order, with the additional difficulty that the set of vehicles to be coordinated changes as traffic flows through the intersection. Since the resulting mixed-integer optimal control problem is hard to solve online, we propose an arrival-triggered receding-horizon scheme built around a schedule-refinement heuristic: for a fixed crossing order, a single nonlinear program (NLP) optimizes all trajectories and crossing times, and the first-order sensitivities of the cost with respect to the vehicle schedule are used to select adjacent swaps that are likely to reduce the overall cost. Replanning is triggered only when a new vehicle arrives, the new vehicle is appended at the tail of the current crossing order, and a memory of evaluated swaps that persists across replanning steps avoids redundant computations. Simulations of traffic scenarios involving streams of a few hundred heterogeneous vehicles show that the proposed scheme recovers most of the optimality gap incurred by first-in-first-out scheduling.

items.title: Real-Time Coordination of Autonomous Vehicles at Intersections
items.summary: When coordinating connected and automated vehicles at an unsignalized intersection, the crossing order and the vehicle trajectories must be decided jointly. For a fixed crossing order, the problem can be formulated conveniently in a bi-level form where each vehicle solves its own optimal control problem, whose optimal value is a function of its entry and exit times, and a coordinator optimizes these times subject to precedence constraints. We compute the first and second order sensitivities of lower-level problems, which are required to solve the upper-level problem, by means of algorithmic differentiation using the real-time software package \texttt{acados}. This implementation exploits tailored algorithms to obtain a computationally efficient implementation of the optimal coordination algorithm. We validate our implementation in numerical simulations that demonstrate both real-time feasibility and effectiveness of our algorithm.

items.title: Beyond Alignment: Whitening Geometry, Profile Synthesis, and Heterogeneous Ensembles for Cross-Environment WiFi Action Recognition
items.summary: Cross-environment deployment is the central obstacle to practical WiFi sensing: a pipeline reaching 0.89+ top-1 in its training environments collapses to 0.408 under Leave-One-Domain-Out (LODO) evaluation with only K-shot labels. A ceiling analysis shows the collapse is not an alignment problem: the action signal is strong across seen environments (about 0.89 K10), environment identity is decodable from the encoder (0.965), and the failure concentrates in the encoder's extrapolation to the novel environment. A pre-registered falsification chain confirms that "align the domains" methods--training-time alignment, readout-level prototype alignment, adversarial confusion, and covariance/subspace alignment (CORAL -3.8pp, subspace -8.3pp)--degrade performance, and that source-domain statistics anti-correlate with cross-environment contribution. The effective levers lie elsewhere; we combine them into Dec-H: (i) closed-form source within-class whitening, provably re-geometrizing the readout's L2 regularization (+8.6pp, zero cost); (ii) profile-mixing augmentation (+1.0pp); (iii) few-shot adaptation with alternating whitening refit (+1.5pp; fixed preconditioners are 20/20 negative); (iv) heterogeneous decision ensembles (+1.7pp); homogeneous scaling and source-weighted stacking are saturated or harmful. Dec-H reaches 0.560 K10 (0.812 K40), +15.2pp over the baseline, consistent across all four environments and seeds; all thirteen configurations were pre-registered with frozen criteria.

items.title: A Heuristic for Scheduling Autonomous Vehicles at Intersections
items.summary: We consider the coordination of autonomous vehicles at unsignalized intersections, where trajectory planning and crossing-order decisions are intrinsically coupled, thereby making their simultaneous optimization intractable in practice. To this end, we propose a heuristic based on a hierarchical structure consisting of a series of nonlinear programs (NLP) in the lower level, which optimizes trajectories of each vehicle for a given crossing order, and a high-level heuristic to design new crossing schedules that exploits sensitivity information from the lower-level NLPs. Extensive numerical simulations across a broad range of traffic scenarios demonstrate that our strategy achieves substantially improved scheduling with respect to first-in-first-out ordering while preserving computational tractability.

items.title: Personalized Privacy-Aware MARL Offloading in the Edge-Cloud Continuum
items.summary: Task offloading in End-Edge-Cloud computing enables resource-constrained User Devices (UDs) to execute computation-intensive applications with reduced latency and energy consumption. However, existing task offloading schemes generally overlook the heterogeneous privacy requirements of users, leading to inefficient privacy-aware offloading decisions. In this paper, we propose a personalized privacy-aware task offloading framework, where the privacy requirement of each task is quantified through a User-Centric Privacy (UCP) model that considers task sensitivity, user privacy preferences, and task urgency. The task offloading problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) to jointly optimize the offloading ratio and the target computing server while minimizing the long-term system cost under latency, energy, and privacy constraints. To efficiently solve the resulting high-dimensional continuous optimization problem, we develop an Advantage-Weighted Actor-Critic (AWAC)-enhanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) algorithm under the Centralized Training and Decentralized Execution (CTDE) paradigm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves lower average system cost, lower energy consumption, and higher task success rate than representative baselines under diverse privacy requirements.

items.title: Signed Powers-of-Two Greedy Vector Approximation of Zadoff-Chu Sequences
items.summary: This paper explores the use of sums of signed powers-of-two (SOPOT) for a representation suitable for multiplierless applications of ZC sequences, where multiplications are reduced to a prescribed number of shift-and-add operations. The SOPOT representation is achieved using a greedy algorithm that outperforms other approaches for multiplierless approximations, such as CORDIC and CSD. The proposed algorithm is based on the matching pursuits using generalized bit planes (MPGBP), and the proposed modification enables robustness to hyperparameter tuning. The resulting sequences retain, to some extent, the good autocorrelation properties of ZC, as shown in a matched-filter detection simulation. This corroborates to their use in various practical applications across mainstream cellular systems and devices requiring moderate computational cost.

items.title: A Continuous Payload-Bearing Discrete Multitone Modulation Framework for Fiber-Optic Integrated Sensing and Communication
items.summary: A key challenge in fiber-optic integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is to make the payload-bearing waveform itself serve both functions without a separate sensing waveform or sensing-only silent interval. We propose a continuous discrete multitone (DMT) framework with two waveform modes, in which the same payload-bearing waveform supports forward intensity-modulation/direct-detection (IM/DD) communication and backward distributed acoustic sensing (DAS). A unified phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry (φ-OTDR) model represents distributed Rayleigh backscattering as a finite-memory sensing multipath channel. It shows that conventional pulse-and-wait φ-OTDR requires a round-trip-time-scale silent interval to isolate successive returns, while nonzero off-peak samples in practical matched-filter (MF) pulse compression cause spatial intersymbol interference (ISI). Continuous DMT instead retains superposed returns and separates range-cell contributions through known-waveform channel reconstruction. Cyclic-prefix DMT (CP-DMT) uses a full-memory CP and one-tap frequency-domain equalization (FDE); under sufficient-CP and ideal full-bin inversion conditions, it eliminates MF-correlation-induced spatial ISI. Cyclic-prefix-free DMT (NoCP-DMT) applies regularized least squares (LS) to the long-memory linear convolution, avoiding the CP at higher receiver complexity. Experiments over a 10-km fiber link localize a 600-Hz disturbance applied by a piezoelectric transducer (PZT) near 5.071 km and recover gauge-differential phase with correlations of 0.989 and 0.987 for CP-DMT and NoCP-DMT, respectively. At 2- and 1-V PZT drive levels, the ten-record localization standard deviations are 0.16/0.11 m and 0.18/0.38 m, respectively. The corresponding IM/DD error vector magnitude values range from 4.80% to 5.00%, with no bit errors observed.

items.title: Self-Supervised Operator Learning for Channel Estimation in Fluid Antenna Systems
items.summary: Fluid antenna systems (FAS) have emerged as a promising technology for enhancing wireless communications through adaptive antenna repositioning. Recently, Fourier neural operators (FNOs) have shown strong potential for FAS channel estimation owing to their ability to learn resolution-invariant mappings and generalize across different port densities. However, existing operator learning approaches require densely sampled channel realizations as training labels, whereas a practical receiver only collects noisy pilot observations from a small subset of ports. This mismatch between training requirements and practical channel acquisition poses a major obstacle to deployment. To address this challenge, we develop a self-supervised framework that trains the FNO-based estimator directly from noisy sub-sampled pilots without any labeled channel fields. The proposed objective combines a pilot splitting strategy, which creates supervision at ports hidden from the model input, with a correction based on Stein's unbiased risk estimate (SURE) that eliminates the measurement noise bias. We prove that this objective admits the same minimum mean square error (MMSE) solution as the ideal supervised criterion. Since the loss relies solely on received pilots, the estimator can be continually adapted online on the live pilot stream. Simulation results show that the self-supervised FNO achieves accuracy comparable to supervised training, generalizes zero-shot to unseen port resolutions, and rapidly recovers from distribution shift via online adaptation.

items.title: A closed-loop agentic research environment for MRI development within Siemens IDEA platform
items.summary: Motivation: Testing new ideas in MRI can require substantial effort to learn sequence programming and reconstruction tools and to debug implementations before the scientific question can be addressed. Goals: Reduce the implementation and debugging burden of testing MRI ideas while retaining researcher control of scientific decisions. Approach: We developed an environment where LLM agents develop sequences in the native Siemens IDEA platform, evaluate them through Bloch simulation and reconstruction, and further iteratively refine them using scanner feedback. Results: As test cases, the agentic environment was used to implement and validate a GIRF-based gradient-calibration sequence and reconstruction in approximately 4 hours, and to develop and optimize a rapid 3-second multichannel calibration scan in approximately 12 hours of researcher-guided iteration.

items.title: Policy-Conditioned Koopman Representations for Parameterized Closed-Loop Systems
items.summary: Predicting the response of a nonlinear system across different feedback controllers requires a model that captures how the closed-loop dynamics change with the controller parameters. In a finite-dimensional Koopman model, these changes may affect both the latent dynamics and the observable coordinates used to represent them. We propose a policy-conditioned Koopman representation framework to address this problem. It allows a single learned model to predict a family of closed-loop trajectories without retraining for each controller. We test the framework on six nonlinear prediction benchmarks, where the mean error of the model stays below a 15% threshold on every system, while that of each baseline exceeds it on at least one. As an example application, the resulting surrogate supports one-shot feedback-parameter selection, in which an optimization at the initial state selects a controller that then operates with fixed parameters and ongoing state feedback. On nonlinear control benchmarks including MuJoCo, the selected controllers stabilize every system from the tested initial state with 1.4 to 21 times less online computation than nonlinear model predictive control, counting the selection itself. The results show that policy-dependent coordinates can support both prediction across closed-loop systems and controller selection without repeated online trajectory optimization.

items.title: Lightweight Low-Frequency Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring via Karhunen-Loève Feature Distillation and Temporal Convolutional Networks
items.summary: Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) is a critical enabler for demand-side management which allows for smart grid optimization. A deployment-ready NILM solution necessitates three key features: accurate disaggregation, low-frequency sampling, and low computational cost. This paper proposes a lightweight, edge-oriented NILM framework that combines activity-boundary-aware synthetic data augmentation with Karhunen-Loève Transform (KLT) feature extraction and a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN). The augmentation stage extracts and recombines complete or near-complete appliance activation segments so that the model can be trained without new fully labeled household aggregates. The KLT filter bank extracts decorrelated, appliance-informed temporal features which are then fed into a compact TCN along with the original aggregate for energy disaggregation. Evaluations on two standard NILM datasets, UK-DALE and REDD, at 10-s sampling and with leave-one-house-out testing, demonstrate that the proposed architecture achieves comparable or superior disaggregation accuracy relative to NILMFormer, BERT4NILM, BiLSTM, and BiGRU. The computational footprint of the framework is 31,009 parameters, the fewest of the five models compared, and on a single CPU thread it needs 2.78 ms per 1000 samples, 84-95% less than the baselines. These results demonstrate a favorable accuracy-efficiency tradeoff for low-frequency smart-meter NILM.

items.title: DARSY: A Tool for Data-Driven Abstraction and Policy Synthesis for Stochastic Systems with Unknown Dynamics
items.summary: This paper presents DARSY: a software tool for abstraction-based verification and policy synthesis in discrete-time stochastic control systems with unknown dynamics and noise distributions. DARSY requires only a simulator of the system and a Lipschitz bound on its dynamics, and needs no knowledge of dynamics or noise distributions. The tool is fully automated and constructs a finite interval Markov decision process (IMDP) abstraction from sampled transitions, whose probability intervals are obtained via statistical techniques and Lipschitz reasoning. Robust dynamic programming on this IMDP then yields a policy together with a lower bound on the probability that the unknown system satisfies a desired specification. This lower bound holds with a user-specified confidence; that is, it is probably approximately correct (PAC). The tool is implemented in Python and supports general Lipschitz-continuous system dynamics and specifications expressed in syntactically co-safe LTL (scLTL), which includes reach-avoid and finite-horizon safety specifications as special cases. Beyond standard IMDPs, DARSY implements a two-layer IMDP (2IMDP) abstraction that also bounds the probability of transitioning to aggregated state blocks, yielding smaller abstraction errors than IMDP abstractions and, as a result, tighter satisfaction guarantees. We demonstrate DARSY's broad applicability across a variety of benchmarks and specifications.

items.title: MambaLIFT: Reference-Based Mechanism-Aware Attribution for VMamba
items.summary: Attributing predictions of visual state-space models remains challenging because input-dependent selective dynamics couple feature selection, recurrent state propagation, and shared computational pathways. We introduce MambaLIFT, a reference-based, multiplier-first attribution framework for VMamba that propagates contributions through its computational graph using interaction-aware rules for selective-scan injection, recurrent memory, LayerNorm, and shared pathways. MambaLIFT decomposes the reference-relative class-logit difference, \(f_c(x)-f_c(x^0)\), by spatial position, VSS block, scan direction, and computational mechanism. Experiments on ImageNet-1K evaluate VMamba-T and VMamba-B, with hyperparameters selected on a calibration set and faithfulness assessed on a disjoint held-out evaluation set. MambaLIFT achieves numerical conservation to floating-point precision across audited attribution interfaces in both configurations. Under mean-colour pixel flipping, it achieves significantly higher mean faithfulness scores than MambaLRP on both configurations and the highest scores among the evaluated methods, including Integrated Gradients with matched references. Under blurred replacement, MambaLIFT is non-inferior to MambaLRP on VMamba-T and equivalent on VMamba-B, indicating that its advantage depends on the replacement protocol. Ablations on VMamba-T show that interaction allocation, temporal propagation, and pathway composition affect attribution maps. Mechanism-level analyses further show that exact relevance conservation does not imply additive effects under finite interventions: the mechanism decomposition accounts for the reference-relative logit difference but does not estimate intervention effects or establish causal validity.

items.title: QUBO-based feature selection for MRI undersampling pattern design
items.summary: We formulate undersampling mask design for Cartesian magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) as a feature subset selection problem. Each sampling line is represented by a binary feature indicating whether it is included in each candidate mask. Using candidate masks and their training-set evaluations, we estimate mutual information (MI) and conditional mutual information (CMI). These estimates and a sampling-count penalty define a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) model. The model is solved using simulated annealing and quantum annealing to determine a feature subset and its corresponding sampling mask. We assess the selected subsets on the test set through zero-filled reconstruction in Fourier undersampling simulations using fastMRI knee magnitude reference images, with patient-disjoint training and test sets. At all six tested target sampling rates from 15% to 40%, the resulting reconstructions have lower mean root mean square error than those obtained with four conventional sampling methods. They also have higher mean structural similarity than those obtained using univariate mutual-information ranking at all tested rates. These results support information-theoretic feature selection as an approach to MRI undersampling mask design under the tested zero-filled simulation settings.

items.title: UMelCodec: An Ultra-Low-Bitrate and Lightweight Mel-Domain Neural Speech Codec
items.summary: Ultra-low-bitrate speech coding is crucial for bandwidth-constrained communication and compact storage, but preserving intelligibility, naturalness, and fine-grained acoustic details at bitrates of only a few hundred bps remains challenging. Existing purely acoustic codecs generally operate at relatively high bitrates, whereas incorporating semantic representations can reduce the bitrate, but at the cost of increased complexity. Therefore, we propose UMelCodec, a purely acoustic neural speech codec operating in the mel domain at an ultra-low bitrate of 325 bps with a lightweight architecture. UMelCodec consists of two stages. In the first mel-domain coding stage, alias-free Snake-ConvNeXt (AF-SC) encoder-decoder backbones model temporal and harmonic structures, a factorized single-codebook vector quantizer (VQ) enables ultra-low-bitrate quantization, and a multi-scale mel-spectrogram discriminator (MSMD) improves mel-spectrogram reconstruction. In the second waveform synthesis stage, a lightweight modified discrete cosine transform (MDCT)-based neural vocoder predicts the MDCT spectrum from the reconstructed mel spectrogram and recovers the waveform through inverse MDCT. Experiments on LibriTTS dataset demonstrate that UMelCodec outperforms strong baselines across most objective reconstruction metrics while maintaining competitive subjective naturalness. In terms of model complexity and inference efficiency, UMelCodec has only 19.67 M parameters, requires 1.93 G MACs, and supports real-time inference on both GPU and CPU platforms.

items.title: Passing NPCR Without Diffusion: Exact Signatures, a Detection Benchmark and an Audit of Published Image Ciphers
items.summary: NPCR, the share of ciphertext bytes changed by a one-pixel plaintext change, is reported for nearly every image cipher as evidence of diffusion, with 99.61% the target. Several mechanisms produce values near it, and the mean does not say which. We separate three regimes: no propagation, one round of forward and backward chaining linear over addition or XOR, and independent ciphertexts. For the second an exact count applies. After a least-significant-bit change its mean asymptotically matches the independent-ciphertext reference, while its spread without cancellation is about five to twenty times larger. In simulation, the one-sided NPCR test of Wu, Noonan and Agaian flags one-round additive, mixed and S-box chaining in 2-4% of papers; read in both directions, the same five values flag at least 99.9%. Two-sided testing does the detecting; the spread and the other signatures help diagnose the structure. We then audit twenty-one published schemes. The count matches a reimplementation of one published diffusion layer on every trial and accounts for its reported table, the signatures show two schemes whose printed specifications cannot produce their reported values, and find that three of our own report plain-versus-cipher values and fall to two chosen images; ten more change their encryption material with the plaintext or per encryption, so their NPCR mostly reflects that change. A released checker applies the signatures to published tables, showing what a table measures within stated assumptions; it does not certify security.

items.title: An LLM-Orchestrated Agent Framework for CKM-Assisted Network Deployment Optimization
items.summary: Channel knowledge maps (CKMs) offer reusable, site-specific radio priors to facilitate environment-aware network planning. However, deploying heterogeneous network nodes to meet diverse performance requirements in complex environments is challenging and requires executable workflows that coordinate scene preparation, candidate-site specification, CKM construction, optimization, and validation. This paper presents a large language model (LLM)-orchestrated agent framework for CKM-assisted network deployment optimization, where an LLM translates high-level requirements into modular, typed, and reproducible planning workflows. In this framework, an LLM layer interprets intent, selects modules, and populates normalized configurations; physics-grounded modules generate scene, CKM, optimization, and validation artifacts; and a deterministic guarded controller performs validation-guided refinement. A common target-candidate-CKM-optimizer interface supports the registration and composition of compatible planning modules, with CKM backends, samplers, and solvers remaining replaceable. We instantiate the proposed framework for base station (BS) deployment, intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) deployment, and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) trajectory planning. An urban-block case study demonstrates automatic scene consistency checks, bounded BS/IRS deployment refinement, and collision- and radio-feasible UAV planning.

items.title: LBW-NPS: A Local Band-Weighted Noise Power Spectrum Loss for Texture-Preserving Low-Dose CT Denoising
items.summary: Low-dose CT denoising should suppress noise while retaining the local texture of the reference image. Matching a pooled spectrum can overlook regional discrepancies, whereas pixel losses alone can favor overly smooth outputs. We propose a local band-weighted noise power spectrum loss (LBW-NPS) that compares spectral energies within overlapping Hann-tapered patches, without tissue-specific loss conditioning. Each valid patch contributes a weighted squared log-energy difference across three frequency bands, alongside an $L_1$ reconstruction term. We compare LBW-NPS against $L_1$-only training and five auxiliary-loss baselines using the same U-Net and three seeds on DeepLesion slices with simulated low-dose acquisitions, including patch-scale ablations and lung, soft-tissue, and bone evaluations. On 220 test slices from 31 patients, LBW-NPS reduces a local spectral gap related to the loss, on $64\times64$-pixel evaluation windows, by 31.9% relative to pooled band-weighted NPS, without a statistically significant PSNR change. This improvement is supported by lower errors relative to the reference in average NPS frequency and gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) measures not used in the loss, evaluated in homogeneous soft tissue. Local band-power matching therefore improves regional texture agreement without changing the denoising architecture.

items.title: AudioTurbo: Fast Text-to-Audio Generation with Rectified Diffusion
items.summary: Diffusion models have significantly improved the quality and diversity of text-to-audio (TTA) generation but are hindered by slow inference speed. Recent flow-based approaches have been explored for accelerating TTA generation. However, these approaches typically rely on dedicated flow-based generative frameworks and do not directly exploit existing pre-trained diffusion-based TTA models. To address this limitation while leveraging the strong generative capabilities of pre-trained diffusion models, we integrate rectified diffusion into these models to improve TTA generation efficiency. Specifically, we propose AudioTurbo, which learns first-order approximate ordinary differential equation (ODE) paths from deterministic noise-sample pairs generated by a pre-trained TTA model. Experiments show that our approach outperforms a flow-matching-based acceleration model in both generation quality and inference speed.

items.title: Computing Optimal Non-stationary Policies for the Probabilistic Reach-Avoid Problems
items.summary: We develop and analyze an algorithm for computing optimal non-stationary policies for probabilistic reach-avoid problems. The objective in probabilistic reach-avoid problems is to maximize the probability of reaching a goal without visiting predefined avoid states. Prior work has focused on computing optimal stationary reach-avoid policies. Stationary policies use the same action distribution whenever a given state is visited. This paper shows that stationary reach-avoid policies may be suboptimal and non-stationary policies may outperform them in reach probability by a margin arbitrarily close to one. To compute optimal non-stationary policies, we reduce the reach-avoid problem to a constrained average-reward Markov decision problem and propose an algorithm to compute lottery-based policies from a standard linear program formulation. We prove that the lottery-based policies are optimal and show that they are simple to compute, analyze, interpret, and implement. The numerical experiments confirm that the lottery-based policies can outperform state-of-the-art stationary policies even in complex domains.

items.title: Physics-Guided Multi-Output Surrogate Modeling of a Centralized-UPS Data Center
items.summary: Data centers supplied through centralized uninterruptible power supplies (UPSs) are converter-dominated loads whose grid response reflects IT demand, power-conversion controls, energy storage, cooling, and site-support dynamics. This paper develops and electrically realizes a causal multi-output surrogate for a nominal 1-MW, 0.48-kV simulated data center. Four physics-informed terminal features-normalized IT demand, positive-sequence voltage deviation, voltage-unbalance ratio, and frequency deviation-are used to predict active and reactive power at both the point of common coupling (PCC) and UPS output. Six causal surrogate families are evaluated using separate training, validation, and held-out trajectories. A ridge-regularized low-order nonlinear autoregressive model with exogenous inputs (NARX) achieves the lowest validation and test errors, with mean four-output errors of 0.1959\% and 0.1441\% on a 1-MVA base, respectively. The selected surrogate is then coupled to a three-phase electrical interface in MATLAB/Simulink, where predicted PCC active power controls a variable resistive load and predicted reactive power is realized through controlled current sources synchronized to the PCC voltage. Across two 41-s AI workload profiles, including an additional pipeline parallelism trajectory, the electrical realization tracks the NARX commands with active- and reactive-power RMSEs of 0.604 kW and 0.353 kVAR for Evaluation Profile A and 1.539 kW and 0.442 kVAR for Evaluation Profile B, respectively. The results demonstrate a compact terminal surrogate that can reproduce both predicted power trajectories and their corresponding three-phase electrical behavior under measured PCC excitation.

items.title: Life-IQA+: Boosting Blind Image Quality Assessment via GCN-enhanced Layer Interaction and Flexible Hierarchical Expert Specialization
items.summary: Blind image quality assessment (BIQA) is essential for evaluating and optimizing visual experience. Existing BIQA methods typically aggregate features from multiple backbone stages without accounting for their unequal contributions to quality prediction. Furthermore, uniformly supervising all experts may constrain their flexibility and limit the diversity of the learned quality representations. To address these issues, we present Life-IQA+, a quality representation decoding framework that combines graph convolutional network (GCN) enhanced layer interaction and flexible hierarchical expert specialization. Specifically, the layer interaction module constructs quality queries from GCN-refined deepest-stage features and uses penultimate-stage features as keys and values, thereby enabling cross-layer representation interaction via the cross-attention mechanism. Building on these representations, we further introduce a flexible hierarchical mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture comprising a densely activated shared expert layer and a sparsely activated routed expert layer. To enhance the representation diversity and ability of experts, we apply auxiliary classification supervision to a subset of shared experts using distortion-type labels for synthetic datasets and discretized quality-level labels for authentic datasets. Experiments on synthetic and authentic distortion benchmarks, together with controlled ablations of expert configurations and supervision strategies, show that Life-IQA+ achieves competitive prediction accuracy with a favorable balance between accuracy and computational cost. The code is available at: https://github.com/TANGLONG2/Life-IQA-PlusPlus.

items.title: Joint Language Modeling for In-the-Wild Speech-Scene Generation with Distinct Token Representations
items.summary: Speech-scene generation aims to synthesize intelligible target speech together with diverse environmental sounds as a coherent acoustic scene. The task is considered challenging in two respects. Speech and environmental audio differ substantially in their semantic and acoustic characteristics, yet existing approaches typically model the complete scene using a single mixed acoustic representation. At the same time, the two sounds are closely related in real-world speech scenes, whereas conventional approaches usually rely on simulated scenes mixed from independently recorded sources. We propose a large language model (LLM)-based framework for joint modeling of distinct speech and environment token streams. A source-aware neural audio codec extracts temporally aligned speech and environment tokens from mixed audio, and a pretrained LLM generates both token streams in an interleaved fashion conditioned on the natural-language scene description and speech content. This formulation preserves source-specific representations while modeling the token streams within a shared generative context. Since both streams are extracted directly from mixed recordings, the model can also be adapted to in-the-wild speech scenes without isolated sources. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves speech intelligibility, scene relevance, and audio quality over existing speech-scene generation techniques, with consistent gains from real-world adaptation. We further investigate the effects of distinct token representations and interleaved generation, and analyze whether the environmental sound remains stable while speech is active and how the two streams interact.

items.title: Koopman Lifting for Linear Encrypted Control of Nonlinear Systems: Applications to LQR and MPC
items.summary: Homomorphic encryption enables control computations to be outsourced to a third-party cloud server without disclosing measurements or controller parameters. Applying existing encrypted linear controllers to nonlinear plants requires a compatible representation of the plant dynamics. This paper presents Homomorphically Encrypted Koopman-Based Control (HEK-Control), which connects nonlinear plants to encrypted linear computations through Koopman lifting. A trusted plant-side client evaluates nonlinear functions of the measured state, and a linear predictor identified in these coordinates supports conventional controller design. The resulting control laws retain the server's encrypted linear operations. We demonstrate the framework using state feedback based on linear quadratic regulation and input-constrained model predictive control. Closed-loop simulations with the Cheon--Kim--Kim--Song encryption scheme show close agreement with unencrypted computations. Additional unencrypted simulations compare regulation under input constraints across a common set of controller designs. For a continuous stirred-tank reactor, Koopman lifting supports regulation at input bounds not handled by the tested controllers designed directly in the original state coordinates. Tests of encrypted computations also show that packing multiple values into each ciphertext reduces computation time and communication volume. These results clarify how existing encrypted linear computations can serve nonlinear plants.

items.title: Distributed Regenerative Resource Allocation with Exact Centralized Optimality
items.summary: This letter presents a Distributed Regenerative Resource Allocation (or DRRA) framework for multi-agent networks with utility-driven resource regeneration, in which the resource available for the next allocation round depends endogenously on the utility generated by the agents in the previous allocation. We develop fully distributed, two-stage inner--outer dynamics that perform primal--dual allocation and resource regeneration. Under sufficient distributed algorithmic gain conditions, the inner dynamics exhibit local exponential convergence to a Lyapunov-stable equilibrium. After inner convergence, the DRRA allocation exactly recovers the centralized optimum, and the local resource-reference updates exactly reproduce the centralized resource-regeneration dynamics.

items.title: Motion-Sickness-Aware Vehicle Control via DKUC-Based Inverse Design and Iterative Feedback Tuning
items.summary: Tuning existing vehicle controllers for motion-sickness reduction requires a desired vehicle response that reflects physiological comfort. The six-degree-of-freedom subjective vertical conflict (6DoF-SVC) model can evaluate sensory conflict induced by vehicle motion, but it does not directly provide a target motion for controller design. This paper proposes a 2-step framework to construct such a reference. First, a target SVC trajectory is generated from the baseline response by limiting conflict peaks while imposing a minimum activity level. Second, a lifted linear model identified using Deep KoopmanU with Control (DKUC) is inverted to map the target SVC trajectory to a regularized reference expressed in vehicle-acceleration and angular-velocity coordinates. The resulting motion reference is then used in an Iterative Feedback Tuning (IFT)-style procedure for fixed-structure PI and LQR controllers. In the considered simulation scenario, the selected SVC target reduces the sequence norm by 6.95\% relative to the baseline. Controller tuning with reduced response models decreases the regularized PI and LQR objectives by 49.5\% and 32.3\%, respectively. These results show that a nonlinear physiological comfort objective can be converted into a practical motion reference for tuning fixed-structure vehicle controllers.

items.title: AIstatLab at BraTS-GoAT 2026 Task 3: Quality-Controlled Consensus Pseudo-Labeling and Dense Expert Adaptation
items.summary: BraTS-GoAT Task 3 evaluates brain-tumor segmentation across heterogeneous entities using shared ET, TC, and WT regions. We present a 3D ResidualEncoderUNet trained with quality-controlled consensus pseudo-labels, a training-only nested-region objective, and a four-expert bottleneck adapter. Five-fold ResEnc-M/L teachers gener ated predictions for 1,138 unlabeled cases; fusion, hierarchy enforcement, and confidence-and-agreement screening retained 983 for training with 1,351 annotated cases. The final five-fold ResEnc-M entry achieved mean DSC 0.834, mean NSD 0.510, and Acalc = 0.6720 on the validation server. Component effects were modest and region-dependent, with the clearest gains on ET. Source code is available at https://github.com/HeeSeung-Shin/Brats2026-Goat-HS.

items.title: A four-level executable validation protocol for evaluating LLM-generated topology specifications of physics-based HVAC digital twins
items.summary: Physics-based digital twins of air conditioning, a principal energy consumer in manufacturing and buildings, can be generated automatically from a declarative specification of its equipment, connections, and sizing. Large language models (LLMs) now write such specifications from plain-language descriptions. Evaluations of these specifications stop at parse success, completed runs, or textual similarity, and cannot reject a model that converges in simulation but is physically wrong. In this study, a four-level protocol is proposed that tests whether an LLM-written specification not only executes but also yields a physically valid digital twin. Each specification is executed through static validity, model build, simulation convergence, and behavioral equivalence with a hidden reference model within bands calibrated by $\pm$20% sizing perturbations. The protocol was applied to eight LLMs and fourteen HVAC topologies, five describing an existing low-humidity test chamber. To test for authorship bias, engineers and a second model family also described six topologies. Within three repairs, seven of eight models built in 98.6 to 100% of trials, with simulations converging in at least 80.0%, but reached behavioral equivalence in only 50.0 to 98.6%. About half of the failed trials converged, but not to the reference steady state, mostly in desiccant rotor systems. Pooled pass rates varied by under five percentage points across description authors. These results imply that the physics hardest to model in each field, here the desiccant rotor, must enter the generation framework as validation levels. The protocol can be adapted to other fields that generate executable digital twins from declarative specifications.

items.title: DeoPC: Data-Enabled Output-Feedback Predictive Control for State Regulation
items.summary: Constrained regulation of the internal state of an unknown linear system is challenging when only input-output measurements are available online. In this work, we develop a data-enabled output-feedback predictive control (DeoPC) framework for constrained state regulation using input-output data. Specifically, a data-driven state estimate is constructed from past input-output data via a subspace-based singular value decomposition. Based on this state representation, we formulate a predictive controller that directly penalizes the state and control effort while enforcing the system constraints. Under persistent excitation and initialization conditions, we establish recursive feasibility and closed-loop stability of DeoPC in both noise-free and bounded-noise settings. In addition, we show that DeoPC can be calibrated to the physical state coordinates using a few offline state measurements, or treated as a model predictive control tuning problem when no state measurements are available. The effectiveness of DeoPC is demonstrated through simulations on an unstable batch reactor system.

items.title: Cone-Constrained Safe Policy Learning With Finite-Step Improvement Guarantees
items.summary: One central challenge in safe reinforcement learning is improving task performance while reducing infeasibility risk, especially when long-term constraint consequences are difficult to represent and optimize. We propose the Constraint Aggregation Function (CAF), a learnable feasibility-oriented representation of long-horizon risk that satisfies a discounted Bellman recursion and admits a unique fixed point. The proposed CAF induces a risk advantage that measures the reduction in predicted unsafety relative to the current policy. Building on this representation, we develop Cone-Constrained Policy Optimization (CCPO), which uses the CAF-induced risk advantage to define a risk descent direction. The proposed CCPO resolves conflicts between task ascent and risk descent through gradient projection, selecting the final update from the relative interior of a constructed safety cone. Under standard smoothness assumptions and a step-size bound, this update guarantees simultaneous task improvement and risk reduction. Numerically, CCPO stays feasible with a 1.05% mean optimality gap in emergency braking and attains low constraint violations on safety-critical benchmarks.

items.title: WiFo-D: Wireless Foundation Model Based on Discrete Representations
items.summary: Wireless foundation models have shown strong generalization capabilities across heterogeneous wireless tasks and configurations. However, most existing models rely on continuous representations, limiting ultra-low-overhead channel state information (CSI) feedback, few-shot generalization, and robustness to noise. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a wireless foundation model based on discrete representations (WiFo-D), which learns multi-granularity discrete CSI representations. It comprises a CSI encoder, multi-codebook vector quantization, and a modulation-based decoder, with the learned token maps and quantized features supporting multi-rate CSI feedback, CSI reconstruction, and diverse CSI-related downstream tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate strong CSI feedback performance at an ultra-low latent compression ratio of 1/32 with 3 bits per token, reducing normalized mean square error (NMSE) by more than 4.7 dB compared with the strongest baseline. Furthermore, for frequency-domain prediction with limited training samples, WiFo-D improves generalization and noise robustness over continuous-representation-based methods. The results also demonstrate its superiority across downstream tasks, including beam prediction, wireless localization, and line-of-sight/non-line-of-sight identification.

items.title: Angel: Anchor-Structured Neural Gaussians for Explicit Fetal Diffusion MRI Slice-to-Volume Reconstruction with Cross-Subject Learning
items.summary: Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) provides a noninvasive view of developing tissue microstructure and white matter tracts in the fetal brain. During acquisition, however, fetal motion disrupts spatial correspondence between slices, diffusion encoding directions and signal intensities. We introduce ANGEL, an anchor-structured neural Gaussian framework for accurate slice-to-volume reconstruction (SVR) of fetal dMRI, that simultaneously estimates diffusion signal, fetal motion and intensity artefacts. Unlike standard explicit Gaussian representation, ANGEL is designed to prevent absorption of noise and artefacts into the reconstructed dMRI by learning a compact representation of spatio-angular signal via a shared decoder that predicts 3D Gaussians across anchors and subjects. The individual anatomical variability is compactly represented through subject-specific anchors. Experiments on simulated neonatal and in vivo fetal data show significant improvement of dMRI reconstruction in both spatial and angular domains, in comparison to explicit Gaussian representation, implicit neural representation as well as classical methods.

items.title: Data-Driven Hamiltonian Under Parametric Uncertainty
items.summary: Hamilton--Jacobi (HJ) reachability computes the states from which a system can be kept out of an unsafe region, but it requires knowledge of dynamics. The data-driven Hamiltonian (DDH), under a black-box dynamics setting, lower bounds the Hamiltonian directly from trajectory data, which produces a guaranteed conservative safe set. However, it needs a Lipschitz constant of the dynamics, and its bound loosens with the distance from the data. We consider dynamics that are linear in unknown parameters through a known feature vector, with a Gaussian prior on the parameters, and use this structure to construct a parametric DDH. From a few short trajectories with noisy velocity measurements, the parametric DDH lower-bounds the Hamiltonian at all states and costates with a probability of at least $1-δ$. The safe set obtained by replacing the Hamiltonian with this bound is then contained in the true safe set with the same probability. For control-affine systems, evaluating the bound amounts to a second-order cone program, so it can be solved efficiently within existing grid-based and neural PDE solvers. We demonstrate the approach on a two-state system and a six-state lunar lander.

items.title: Orchestrating Wheeled Mobile Robots Online without Conflicts
items.summary: Formation control of wheeled mobile robots (WMRs) has been widely studied due to its broad applications. However, existing studies primarily focus on tracking predefined formations, with limited adaptability to varying environments. To address this limitation, we propose CFOO, a Conflict-Free Online Orchestration framework for continuous formation navigation of WMRs that integrates centralized formation generation with distributed formation maintenance. The upper layer monitors the environment in real time and generates adaptive formations as needed, using the proposed TCF-R2T (Trajectory-Conflict-Free Robot-to-Target assignment) algorithm to compute optimal assignments in polynomial time for timely, conflict-free formation transitions. At the lower layer, each WMR continuously employs JSTP (Joint Spatio-Temporal trajectory Planning) to maintain the given formation by jointly optimizing spatial positions and segment durations, improving coordination over spatial-only optimization with fixed durations. By coordinating these two layers, CFOO orchestrates WMRs to adapt their formations to varying environments and thus enable continuous navigation. Moreover, we design a Time-Varying Formation Reference (TVFR) mechanism to facilitate smooth transitions between successive desired formations. Both simulation and real-world experiments validate the effectiveness and adaptability of CFOO. Experimental videos are available on our project website: https://dongjh20.github.io/CFOO.

items.title: TransGHOST: Real-Time, Synthesis-Free Reconstruction of Instrument-Occluded Regions in Ophthalmic Microsurgery
items.summary: Intraoperative scene perception in ophthalmic microsurgery is limited by instrument occlusion: when a tool enters the high-magnification field, it conceals tissue from both the surgeon and the perception components of robot-assisted systems that process the video. Generative inpainting can remove the occluder but replaces the missing image content with synthesis, which is unsuitable when visual provenance matters. Many video inpainters also depend on future frames and cannot operate online. We present TransGHOST, a causal reference-guided reconstruction pipeline whose non-generative safe mode operates in real time. Every restored value is obtained by resampling a recorded frame using geometric transforms fitted only to visible regions. The system provides per-pixel confidence and provenance and marks unsupported pixels as abstentions. We evaluate TransGHOST on a new veterinary clinical corpus of canine cataract surgery with pixel-level instrument and anatomy labels. Only the occluded region is scored, and each scoring target is verified to differ from the reference supplied to the system. Safe mode reaches 31.89 dB masked PSNR and 0.915 masked SSIM at 51.7 ms median and 85.5 ms 95th-percentile latency. On a pre-declared held-out cohort using instrument cutouts excluded from segmentation training, it reaches 29.83 dB masked PSNR, while matched-mask evaluation on validation shows a 3.45 dB advantage over LaMa. Region-aware reference selection improves masked PSNR by 3.60 dB over recency when candidate references can themselves be occluded. Reference-age analysis further defines the operating interval for the brief, repeated occlusions targeted by TransGHOST.

items.title: Breaking Noise Shortcuts in Self-Supervised Learning Via Noise-Aligned View Generation
items.summary: Self-supervised learning (SSL) is increasingly applied to scientific imaging domains, such as microscopy, where labels are scarce but noisy data is abundant. These domains exhibit significant signal-dependent noise, which can create a representational shortcut: since both augmented views derive from the same noisy image, the encoder can boost view agreement by also encoding noise patterns rather than semantic content. To enable noise-robust representation learning without knowledge of underlying noise models, we introduce Self-Aligned Noise Augmentation (SEANA), a drop-in module that generates noise-aware SSL views. SEANA learns an invertible variance-stabilizing transform (VST) from noisy data, then estimates the clean signal and resamples independent noise in learned VST space, requiring no clean targets, no dataset-specific denoiser training or use at inference, and no changes to the SSL objective or encoder. On CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-100 under synthetic Gaussian, Poisson-Gaussian, and multiplicative noise, SEANA improves clean-test linear-probe accuracy across contrastive/non-contrastive SSL methods, indicating higher-quality representations. On real fluorescence imaging, SEANA improves Jurkat cell-cycle stage classification by up to 28.6pp over standard SSL and 27.5pp over denoiser-preprocessed baselines. In all settings, SEANA outperforms the denoiser-preprocessed SSL pipelines, demonstrating that learned VST-space noise-aligned resampling yields more robust representations than denoising alone. Code is available at: https://github.com/opatil31/SEANA

items.title: Improving Imitation Policies for Multi-Phase Tasks through Residual Learning Allocation
items.summary: Residual reinforcement learning corrects an imitation-trained base policy using a limited budget of environment interaction. In a task with several phases, this budget must be divided among the phases, and the phase in which the base policy fails is not necessarily the phase in which a correction most improves task completion. We formalize this distinction through the completion gain: the change in full-task completion probability when, during a single phase, a state-feedback controller replaces selected components of the base policy's action. We decompose the completion gain into the probability of reaching the phase and the conditional improvement in completion from the start of the phase, and we estimate it from paired episodes. The positive estimates determine which action components the residual policy corrects and how training episodes are distributed across phases. In stochastic point-mass docking experiments, most failures occurred in the final docking phase, whereas the largest completion gain occurred in the preceding channel phase; gain-based allocation improved completion over allocation proportional to failure counts and, in a variant with a longer approach, over uniform allocation at half of the budget. In simulated bimanual robotic assembly, the completion-gain estimates were positive only for insertion and release, although few failures occurred during release; in a second assembly configuration, a residual policy trained in the release phase improved completion from held-out states at the start of release by 16.9%.

items.title: The Prediction-to-Decision Gap: First-Action Informativity in Data-Driven Predictive Control
items.summary: Model predictive control (MPC) applies only the first input of an optimized sequence before replanning. Do the available data determine this input? We define first-action informativity as agreement across data-compatible models at a fixed history and reference, with common MPC settings. For autoregressive models with exogenous inputs (ARX) and unconstrained quadratic MPC, we show that first-action agreement and prediction agreement under a fixed input sequence do not imply one another. We give structural conditions for action agreement without requiring unique model identification. When actions disagree, we quantify their mean-squared deviation from the fitted model's input under a specific parameter distribution. We approximate this measure using local sensitivities and parameter covariance. Analytical and numerical examples illustrate how model uncertainty affects predictions and actions differently. The framework evaluates model uncertainty through its effect on the first action MPC is about to apply.

items.title: UHD Low-Light Image Enhancement via Real-Time Enhancement Methods with Clifford Information Fusion
items.summary: Considering efficiency, ultra-high-definition (UHD) low-light image restoration is extremely challenging. Existing methods based on Transformer architectures or high-dimensional complex convolutional neural networks often suffer from the "memory wall" bottleneck, failing to achieve millisecond-level inference on edge devices. To address this issue, we propose a novel real-time UHD low-light enhancement network based on geometric feature fusion using Clifford algebra in 2D Euclidean space. First, we construct a four-layer feature pyramid with gradually increasing resolution, which decomposes input images into low-frequency and high-frequency structural components via a Gaussian blur kernel, and adopts a lightweight U-Net based on depthwise separable convolution for dual-branch feature extraction. Second, to resolve structural information loss and artifacts from traditional high-low frequency feature fusion, we introduce spatially aware Clifford algebra, which maps feature tensors to a multivector space (scalars, vectors, bivectors) and uses Clifford similarity to aggregate features while suppressing noise and preserving textures. In the reconstruction stage, the network outputs adaptive Gamma and Gain maps, which perform physically constrained non-linear brightness adjustment via Retinex theory. Integrated with FP16 mixed-precision computation and dynamic operator fusion, our method achieves millisecond-level inference for 4K/8K images on a single consumer-grade device, while outperforming state-of-the-art (SOTA) models on several restoration metrics.

items.title: Data-driven Linearization of Operational Dynamics of Soft Open Points in Power Distribution Networks
items.summary: This paper proposes a novel data-driven linearization of operational power losses in a Soft Open Point (SOP). The proposed learning-based representation, combined with the standard segmentation of the quadratic device capacity inequalities, linearizes the operational dynamics of SOPs in unbalanced power distribution network applications without a significant drop in power loss estimation accuracy. The technique was tested in three applications using a three-phase extension of the IEEE 33-bus network. The case studies include a sizing application for a multi-terminal phase-changing soft open point (PCSOP), an operational optimization application for an active distribution network featuring a PCSOP, and a system simulation engine built for a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) application that trains an agent to optimally dispatch a PCSOP in an unbalanced distribution network. The results of the three case studies were validated against the standard nonlinear AC load-flow representations and point to the efficacy of the proposed solution.

items.title: Conditional-Hierarchical Open-Set Deep Learning for Robust Radio Signals Intelligence
items.summary: This paper proposes an open-set radio-frequency (RF) deep learning (DL) framework that jointly performs conditionally hierarchical multi-level radio signal classification and out-of-distribution (OOD) detection. To exploit image-based classification models, the raw radio samples are transformed into time-frequency representations using the short time Fourier transform (STFT) to pre-process the radio signals. A lightweight novel architecture using neural network (CNN), that applies con- ditional hierarchical multi-task classification heads, is introduced, and compared to two baselines including: (1) The conventional convolutional neural network (CNN) and (2) Swin-T model with multitask classification heads, where the model accuracy and complexity perspectives are considered for the comparison. Moreover, to address open-set scenarios, we introduce the fusion of two OOD detectors each of which is fitted to a Gaussian mixture model by using the learned feature space (e.g. the feature embeddings and logits) from the multi-head classifica- tion network. The overall training process is achieved on two stages following a post-hoc design: the in-set classification neural network is trained first, then the learnable parameters are frozen in the evaluation mode to process the training dataset again to aggregate the embeddings and logits used to fit the GMMs for OOD detection. Moreover, a proof of concept using experimental setup is implemented to validate the operation of the introduced models and algorithms in practical scenarios. The simulation- based trained model is fine-tuned using experimentally measured radio signals. For the experimental setup, a USRP-B210 acting as a transmitter, and an edge Deepwave Air-T software-defined radio, which is equipped with the fine-tuned neural networks is used as a detector or receiver.

items.title: DS3M: Deep structured state space models for nonlinear system identification on modern hardware
items.summary: Neural state-space identification learns dynamical models from measured inputs and outputs. SUBNET combines this task with an encoder that estimates initial states from short measurement histories. Its continuous-time version requires many successive neural-network evaluations during numerical integration, resulting in slow training speed which is a major limitation for practical use cases. We propose deep structured state space models (DS3M), which combine compact nonlinear dynamical components in parallel and in series. Custom GPU kernels implemented with Triton reduce the launch and memory overhead of their sequential evaluation. We explain this construction, describe a port-Hamiltonian variant, and present various benchmark comparisons of accuracy and training time.

items.title: AE-DISC: Automorphism Ensemble Direct-Invocation Successive Cancellation for Low-Latency Decoding
items.summary: Emerging applications in hyper-reliable low-latency communication (HRLLC) demand channel decoders that deliver deterministic performance under stringent latency and reliability constraints. While Polar codes are well suited for this scenario due to their strong error-correction capability, conventional successive cancellation (SC) decoding exhibits inherent serial dependencies that lead to high decoding latency. This paper presents the automorphism ensemble direct-invocation successive cancellation (AE-DISC) decoder, a low-latency framework that enables the concurrent computation of the left and right decoding subtrees in the SC process, yielding substantial speed-ups. By exploiting permutation automorphisms, AE-DISC decoding further improves error-correction performance. Simulation results demonstrate that AE-DISC attains up to 1.4 dB gain over the 5G SC baseline and surpasses layered min-sum (LMS) low-density parity-check (LDPC) decoders at a frame error rate (FER) of $10^{-6}$, while maintaining fixed algorithmic complexity. Both theoretical analysis and application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) synthesis results further show up to 2 times decoding speed-up relative to fast simplified successive cancellation (FSSC).

items.title: A Synthetic Multi-Modal Testbed for Security Stress Testing of Agentic Counter-UAS Systems
items.summary: Agentic cyber-physical systems rely on perception and state estimation to support autonomous decisions. Degraded, inconsistent, or manipulated sensor observations can therefore propagate through an autonomous pipeline and create security-relevant failures. This work presents a synthetic Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System (C-UAS) testbed developed in NVIDIA Isaac Sim for repeatable stress testing of perception and tracking algorithms supporting agentic decision-making. A simplified quadrotor follows scripted trajectories while co-located virtual sensors generate synchronized RGB, RTX LiDAR, and illustrative IR-like observations. The testbed varies target range, motion, clutter, occlusion, and sensor availability, with future stress cases including sensor dropout, temporal misalignment, cross-modal disagreement, and false observations. As an initial exemplar, a nonlinear coordinated-turn Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) is evaluated over a 20-s maneuvering trajectory using LiDAR target-centroid measurements. Position error and uncertainty are compared as LiDAR observations degrade and are lost. The framework provides a reproducible environment for studying how sensing degradation affects downstream autonomous estimation and resilience in agentic C-UAS systems.

items.title: ConDR: Conservative Reachability through Neural Hamilton-Jacobi Subsolutions
items.summary: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) Reachability identifies the unsafe states of a dynamical system from which it can be forced into failure under worst-case disturbance. However, classical grid-based solvers scale exponentially with state dimension. DeepReach improves scalability by replacing the grid with a neural value function trained on the HJ-Isaacs (HJI) variational inequality (VI), but penalizes both sides of the residual equally. This allows the learned value to lie above the true one and unsafe states to be misclassified as safe. We propose Conservative DeepReach (ConDR) which aims to learn a subsolution of the HJI VI such that the learned unsafe set contains the true one. ConDR enforces the obstacle branch and terminal condition by construction, pushes the HJI residual to a safety margin $ε$ below zero with a one-sided loss, and prevents the degenerate solution of classifying everything as unsafe. We prove that the exact solution of the margin-shifted VI that ConDR trains toward is a subsolution of the original VI so its unsafe set contains the true one and its value lies within $ετ$ of the true value function. We compare against DeepReach and MADR in the established systems of Air3D, Air6D, a 9D multi-vehicle system, and a 13D quadrotor. ConDR reports the lowest rate of unsafe state misclassified and the lowest closed-loop collision rates with at most a small increase in intervention. On Air3D and Air6D, ConDR tolerates model mismatch that scales with $ε$. At matched false-negative rates, ConDR's unsafe sets are smaller than the baselines showing the safety is not obtained by trivial over-approximation.

items.title: Stochastic Crew Placement for Winter Storm Restoration of Rural Distribution Feeders Considering Building Cooling Deadlines
items.summary: Winter storm outages on rural distribution feeders may leave electrically heated houses cooling below acceptable indoor temperatures. This paper proposes a two-stage stochastic mixed-integer linear program for pre-storm crew placement that considers the building cooling deadline. Crews are placed before the storm, and repairs and reconnection are scheduled in each damage scenario to minimize the expected cost. Specifically, outage house-hours beyond the deadline are penalized, and feeder voltage and loading constraints account for cold load pickup at each reconnection. A case study on a synthetic rural feeder shows that the penalty shifts one of two crews toward a remote village, reducing expected house-hours beyond the deadline by 39 percent for 5.3 percent more outage house-hours. With three crews, the penalty does not change crew placement. Immediate reconnection would violate the voltage limit in four of six scenarios.

items.title: From Self-Play RL to Constrained Control: Distilling DiffMPC Students with DAgger
items.summary: Self-play reinforcement learning (RL) produces strong driving policies, but these policies are hard to verify or interpret. Differentiable model predictive control (DiffMPC) can enforce explicit constraints, but it is usually trained by imitating logged data or with costly RL.
